articles.title: ED freezes ₹18.36 crore and 242 bank accounts Exalogic-CMRL payoff case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The ED froze ₹18.36 crore in 242 accounts following raids conducted on Wednesday as part of an alleged pay-off case involving T. Veena, daughter of Kerala's Leader of the Opposition, Pinarayi Vijayan. The searches targeted premises linked to Ms. Veena and the management of the CMRL (Kannur Metro Rail Limited) in Kerala and Bengaluru.  The ED is investigating proceeds of crime generated by the CMRL, led by S.N. Sasidharan Kartha, along with Ms. Veena. The investigation stems from previous findings by the Income Tax department that revealed fake expenses amounting to ₹130 crore.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged pay-off case involving a political leader's family raises concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Fruit vendor found dead in Tirupattur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: L. Santhammal, a 68-year-old fruit vendor from Tirupattur, was found murdered inside a government egg procurement godown near the office of the Deputy Superintendent of Police on Wednesday.  Initial investigations suggest she had been waiting in the godown before visiting her daughters' home due to heavy rain. Superintendent of Police (SP) Akshay Anil Wakhare inspected the scene and fingerprint experts and sniffer dogs are assisting with the investigation. A case has been registered, and special teams have been formed to apprehend suspects.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Murder of a citizen inside a government building raises serious security concerns.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: Madhya Pradesh HC quashes anticipatory bail of retired judge Giribala Singh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has quashed the anticipatory bail granted to retired Bhopal district judge Giribala Singh in the Twisha Sharma dowry harassment and death case. The court, citing inconsistencies in the evidence and lack of remorse from Ms. Singh, ruled that the trial court did not adequately consider the prosecution's claims.  The CBI, which took over the investigation, is expected to arrest Ms. Singh soon for custodial interrogation.

articles.title: Catholic priest said ‘we are but men’ when challenged over sex with spiritual directee, court hears | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Texas court is hearing testimony in the trial of Anthony Odiong, a former Catholic priest accused of sexually assaulting multiple women he met while providing spiritual guidance.  Odiong, 57, has pleaded not guilty to five charges of first-degree and two counts of second-degree sexual assault. The son of one of his alleged victims testified that he witnessed Odiong having sex with his mother at a party in 2011.  The son's testimony was corroborated by the testimony of another woman, who claimed she endured an abusive marriage and was coerced into engaging in sexual acts with her husband by Odiong. The trial is expected to continue through Monday.

articles.title: Queensland man charged with murder after allegedly beating elderly pedestrian to death with pole | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old Bundaberg West man has been charged with murder and attempted murder following a violent rampage in Queensland. The alleged crime spree began when the man reversed his car into a Tesla, then assaulted a driver of a Mitsubishi Pajero before striking a 78-year-old pedestrian with a metal pole. The pedestrian died at the scene, while another victim sustained serious head injuries. Police apprehended the suspect after he allegedly assaulted a 66-year-old man in Childers and were able to arrest him shortly after.

articles.title: Deenthegreat: Kick streamer DeenTheGreat faces felony charge over yacht party incident - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: DeenTheGreat, a popular streamer and influencer boxer, was arrested in Miami-Dade County on Wednesday after an altercation during a yacht party. DeenTheGreat is facing felony attempted robbery charges stemming from an argument with a woman named Destiny Aleman, who claimed he tried to take her phone during the livestream.  Police reviewed Ring camera footage that allegedly showed DeenTheGreat attempting to grab Aleman's phone while she was recording him. The incident has drawn attention online and police are still investigating the case.

articles.title: Former assistant to TV star Matthew Perry sentenced to 41 months in prison | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kenneth Iwamasa, a former assistant to actor Matthew Perry, was sentenced to 41 months in prison for his role in the actor's death from ketamine overdose.  Iwamasa testified that he injected Perry with the drug on October 28th, 2023, at his request. The sentencing concludes the prosecution of five individuals who allegedly facilitated Perry’s death by supplying him with ketamine without proper medical supervision. Keith Morrison, Perry's stepfather, addressed the court, denouncing Iwamasa’s actions and highlighting the potential for intervention.  Perry’s death was ruled an acute effect of ketamine overdose.

articles.title: Excise crackdown: Over 1,200 cases booked; large quantities of illicit liquor, ganja and drugs seized across Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Excise officials in Telangana have conducted a statewide crackdown on illicit liquor, resulting in the booking of 1,218 individuals. The operation, involving joint efforts from the Excise Department, State Task Force (STF), District Task Force (DTF), Enforcement teams, and the Drugs Control Administration (DCA), has led to the seizure of significant quantities of illicit liquor, ganja, and other narcotics.

articles.title: CBI arrests Latur-based doctor and Pune Physics teacher in NEET-UG 2026 case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested two more individuals, Manoj Shirure, a Latur-based doctor, and Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, a physics faculty at Dr Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy (APMA), in connection with the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.  The arrests bring the total number of individuals apprehended to 13. The CBI is continuing its investigation into the conspiracy and chain of events surrounding the leak.

articles.title: Probe incidents of accused being paraded in underwear: APDR writes to West Bengal Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A civil rights organization, the Association of Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR), has filed a complaint with the West Bengal Human Rights Commission alleging that police officers in Howrah district paraded two accused individuals in their underwear and vests. The APDR cites two incidents at Golabari and Sankrail police stations on May 24th and 25th respectively, where the accused were subjected to this treatment.  The organization argues that these actions violate human rights and are a form of "criminal force" by law enforcement.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Public humiliation and undignified treatment by police is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: Twisha Singh death case: Madhya Pradesh HC quashes anticipatory bail of retired judge Giribala Singh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has quashed the anticipatory bail granted to retired Bhopal district judge Giribala Singh in the Twisha Sharma dowry harassment and death case. The court found that the trial court did not consider relevant aspects while granting the bail, and that the respondent, Ms. Singh, had violated the law by making public statements and flouting investigation procedures. The CBI, which took over the case from an SIT of the Bhopal Police, also intervened in the petitions and sought the quashing of the local court's order.  The trial court had granted anticipatory bail to Ms. Singh on May 15 after an FIR was lodged by local police.

articles.title: Woman shot dead outside Sheffield bar had ‘biggest heart’, say family | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Shanice Brookes, a 30-year-old charity worker and mother, was fatally shot outside a bar in Sheffield city centre on Monday. South Yorkshire police have named the suspect as a 30-year-old man and a 32-year-old woman who were arrested near Stockport.  The incident occurred when Brookes was an innocent bystander during an altercation, according to police. Her family described her as "one of a kind" with a "biggest heart". South Yorkshire police are urging anyone with information to come forward.

articles.title: Will file curative petition against youngster’s acquittal from 2017 Mugalivakkam child sexual assault-cum-murder case, T.N. govt. tells Madras High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu government announced its intention to file a curative petition against the Supreme Court's acquittal of an engineering graduate accused of sexually assaulting and murdering a seven-year-old girl in 2017. The Madras High Court recorded the government's submission after a writ petition was filed by advocate S. Venkatesh, who sought a direction to file the curative petition.  The case has been ongoing since 2017 when the accused was sentenced to death by a Chengalpattu court and later confirmed by the Madras High Court. The Supreme Court then acquitted him in October 2025.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The acquittal of a child murderer raises serious concerns about justice.

articles.title: Sexual assault by ex-DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson left witness, then 11, ‘feeling sick’, trial hears | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jeffrey Donaldson, a former MP and Democratic Unionist party leader, is facing 18 sexual offenses charges, including rape, in a high-profile trial in Newry crown court. The accusations span from 1985 to 2008 and involve two alleged victims.  His wife, Eleanor Donaldson, is also charged with aiding and abetting rape and indecent assault. Both deny all the charges.  The trial will last approximately four weeks and include pre-recorded interviews with the complainants, as well as recorded interviews given by the Donaldsons to police after their arrest.

articles.title: Anti-drug surveillance stepped up ahead of school reopening in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police and Excise departments in Ernakulam have intensified anti-drug measures ahead of the reopening of schools.  The District Police Chief (Kochi City), Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar, stated that schools have been instructed to clear their premises of tobacco products and other materials, while District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan warned against selling intoxicating substances near school campuses. The Excise Anti-Narcotics Special Squad seized 18 kg of suspected ganja from a distribution hub in Panambukad, as part of their "Operation Thunder" drive.  The raid was led by Ernakulam Excise Anti-Narcotics Squad Inspector Arun D.S., and officials are searching for Sabu, who allegedly ran the drug network.

articles.title: Police report flags suspected gold thefts at Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple has been the subject of a high-level police intelligence report revealing significant security lapses and suspected thefts. The report, submitted to the Home department, details missing gold bars, a stolen gold lamp, and the disappearance of the sacred 'Vaira Nama' ornament.  The investigation also uncovered instances of security protocol evasion by temple employees, security staff, and associates of the former royal family. The police headquarters has recommended transferring valuables to a centralized strong room, documenting devotee offerings, enforcing strict screening procedures, and implementing a zero-tolerance policy for security bypasses.

articles.title: ‘Wicked lie’: Sikh man’s racism claims challenged in Southampton kirpan murder trial over killing of 18-year-old student - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A jury is deliberating in the case of Vickrum Digwa, accused of murdering 18-year-old Henry Nowak.  Digwa denies murder, manslaughter, and carrying a knife in public. The trial heard evidence including a Snapchat video showing Nowak provoking Digwa before the stabbing. Judge William Mousley KC reviewed testimony about the incident and the legal limits for drink driving. A verdict is expected after deliberations conclude.

articles.title: Kim Soo-hyun: YouTuber arrested for allegedly using AI to defame Korean actor
articles.rephrased_article: Kim Soo-hyun, a popular South Korean actor, has been cleared of defamation accusations after an investigation confirmed the validity of his claims. Kim Se-ui, the YouTuber who made the allegations against him, was arrested for allegedly using AI to create false evidence and manipulate screenshots of text messages.  The Seoul Central District Court granted an arrest warrant for Kim Se-ui citing concerns he might destroy evidence or flee. The actor's agency released a statement stating that "the truth has been proven" and thanked supporters who stood by him.

articles.title: Drunk illegal immigrant driving on wrong side kills 4 people in deadly highway crash in Oklahoma; may face deportation - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Rosario-Cruz, a 27-year-old illegal migrant, has been charged with four counts of second-degree murder after driving the wrong way under the influence on Oklahoma highway I-40, resulting in the deaths of four young people.  The crash occurred early Friday morning and involved a head-on collision that caused the vehicle to catch fire. ICE has issued a detainer request for Rosario-Cruz, who is currently being held at the Canadian County Jail. The victims were identified as Kiercey Hickson, Quincy Jones, Haliegh Salazar, and Brad Palmer.

articles.title: Pothundy twin murder case trial enters final phase - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Additional District and Sessions Court-IV, Palakkad is nearing the end of the trial in the Pothundy twin murder case.  After more than four months of witness examination, the final hearing for Chenthamara, accused of killing Sudhakaran and his mother Lakshmi, has been scheduled for May 29, 2026. The prosecution argues that Chenthamara committed both murders while on parole following a previous conviction for the murder of Sudhakaran's wife Sajitha in 2019.  The case has sparked outrage over the police's alleged failure to prevent the killings despite prior concerns raised by the victims' family.

articles.title: Will accord top priority to safety of women and children: T.N. tells Madras High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's Attorney General, Vijay Narayan, informed the Madras High Court that the government is prioritizing the safety of women and children by developing an action plan to prevent and prosecute sexual crimes against them.  He acknowledged delays in trial completion for such offenses but assured the court that measures are being taken to strengthen police forces and ensure swift justice. The Attorney General stated that a detailed plan would take two to three weeks to develop, including establishing more forensic laboratories. The court issued an interim order directing the Mahila Court in Tiruvannamalai to complete the trial of the PIL petitioner by July 31, 2026.

articles.title: German ex-Red Army Faction militant Daniela Klette jailed for armed robberies after years on the run
articles.rephrased_article: A former member of the German militant group Red Army Faction (RAF), Daniela Klette, was sentenced to 13 years in prison for her involvement in a series of armed robberies between 1999 and 2016.  Klette, who had been on the run for over 30 years, was finally apprehended in Berlin in 2024 after a tip-off to police. Prosecutors allege that Klette was complicit in three of the group's attacks, including a failed bombing at a Deutsche Bank building and a prison bombing.  The trial focused on eight robberies across northern and western Germany, with Klette not explicitly admitting to being an RAF member during the trial but facing further charges related to her alleged involvement in the group's activities.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh DGP defends Bhopal Police as CBI takes over case, launches probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhya Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Kailash Makwana stated that the Bhopal Police followed established procedures in the Twisha Sharma death case, which was subsequently taken over by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).  The family has alleged institutional bias and procedural lapses by local police, including accusations against retired district judge Giribala Singh, who is an accused in the dowry death and harassment case. The CBI team visited Ms. Singh's residence and questioned her while also meeting with the victim’s family members. The High Court will hear petitions challenging Ms. Singh’s anticipatory bail on May 27th.

articles.title: Fast-track court frames charges against seven accused in Zubeen Garg death case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Zubeen Garg, the renowned cultural icon, was found dead in Singapore in September 2025. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that Garg’s death was a result of a conspiracy, while a Singapore coroner's inquiry concluded it was an accidental drowning.  A special fast-track court on Tuesday (May 26, 2026) framed charges against seven accused, including Shyamkanu Mahanta, the event organizer, and Siddharth Sharma, Garg’s manager, for murder. The trial is scheduled to begin on June 8th.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article suggests a potential cover-up of a celebrity's death by powerful figures.

articles.title: Jury seated as US trial of Catholic priest accused of sexual assault begins | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A jury of eight women and four men was selected for the criminal trial of Anthony Odiong, a Roman Catholic priest, who is charged with sexually assaulting three women in Waco, Texas.  Odiong faces five counts of first-degree sexual assault and two counts of second-degree sexual assault. The charges stem from allegations made by several women who accused him of exploiting their emotional dependency for sexual purposes while he was ministering in Texas and Louisiana. Prosecutors will present evidence that Odiong violated the Catholic promise of celibacy, fathered a child with a congregant, and engaged in inappropriate financial control over his accusers.  Odiong's lawyers argue that the state waited too long to file charges against him, introducing hearsay testimony about the number of accusers. The trial is expected to last into next week.

articles.title: 'Unjust and unfounded': Mango founder's son denies killing father, steps down as vice president - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jonathan Andic, son of late Mango founder Isak Andic, has stepped down as vice president of the fashion giant's board to focus on his legal defense after being arrested in Spain as part of an investigation into his father's death.  Andic denies any involvement in his father's death, calling the accusations "serious, unjust and unfounded." The case was reopened in October 2025 after investigators found inconsistencies in Andic's statements and the circumstances surrounding the fall. Authorities are also investigating potential tensions between the father and son related to Isak Andic's plans for a charitable foundation.

articles.title: Woman shot dead outside Sheffield bar was innocent bystander, police say | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Yorkshire police are investigating the fatal shooting of a 30-year-old woman outside a Sheffield bar. The victim, an innocent bystander celebrating the bank holiday weekend, was found with serious injuries and later died in hospital. Ch Supt Jamie Henderson, district commander for Sheffield, stated that two men and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of murder, while police are appealing for witnesses who were in the area around 2:45 am Monday morning.

articles.title: Indian-origin woman killed at supermarket in Virginia; shooter had no connection with her, was later found dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 45-year-old Indian woman, Meghnaben Patel, was fatally shot at a convenience store in Virginia on May 23rd. Surveillance footage shows the attacker approaching the counter where she worked and shooting her multiple times before fleeing.  The shooter died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after being found by police who were responding to reports of a domestic dispute that occurred earlier. Police have not identified any additional suspects in connection with the incident.

articles.title: Inquiry into Post Office Horizon scandal faces five-year delay without extra funding | Post Office Horizon scandal | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Metropolitan police are seeking additional funding and staff to continue their investigation into the Post Office Horizon IT scandal, which has been plagued by delays. Stephen Clayman, the commander in charge of the investigation, stated that a five-year delay is possible without the necessary resources, as they need nearly double the current team size to meet their deadline for submitting files to prosecutors. The investigation, codenamed Operation Olympos, aims to determine if perjury and perverting the course of justice occurred during the prosecution of over 900 post office operators between 1999 and 2015 due to faulty Horizon accounting software from Fujitsu.  The police are awaiting the publication of the second part of the inquiry's findings before moving forward with charging.

articles.title: China executes man for murdering prominent gaming tycoon
articles.rephrased_article: China executed Xu Yao, convicted of poisoning billionaire gaming tycoon Lin Qi in 2020. Lin, founder of Yoozoo Games, died after ingesting poisonous pills disguised as probiotics.  The execution followed a trial where Xu was found guilty of murder and sentenced to death. The incident shocked the gaming industry and left several others ill.

articles.title: Rowdy-sheeter jumps from building to evade arrest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bagalagunte Police Station officers sustained injuries while attempting to arrest a notorious rowdy-sheeter, Nagaraj, who jumped from the first floor of an under-construction building in Soladevanahalli.  The accused suffered serious injuries and was admitted to hospital. He is recovering and police are awaiting his recovery to arrest him. A new case has been filed against Nagaraj for assaulting and obstructing police officers.

articles.title: Police arrest suspect in killing of newly married couple in Karachi's Malir: spokesperson - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Saudabad police arrested the main suspect, Sajid, son of Aslam, in connection with the shooting death of a newly married couple near RCD ground in Malir's Saudabad. The suspect confessed to opening fire on the couple after they returned from court where the woman had recorded her statement about marrying willingly.  A case was registered at Saudabad police station based on the complaint of the deceased husband’s brother, and raids are underway to arrest other suspects involved.

articles.title: Jail authorities request medical examination of alleged drug queenpin Anmol over kidney pain - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Central jail authorities in Karachi requested the Civil Hospital to send a medical team to examine Anmol alias Pinky, an alleged drug queenpin, for kidney issues. The jail superintendent cited security concerns as the reason for not transporting her to the hospital.  The examining physician recommended further evaluation and tests at the Sindh Institute of Urology & Transplantation (SIUT). The police also requested treatment within the prison premises.

articles.title: NT police will not lay charges against officers over Kumanjayi White’s death while being restrained at Coles | Northern Territory | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Northern Territory police will not lay charges against officers involved in the death of Kumanjayi White, a 24-year-old Indigenous man who died while being restrained in an Alice Springs supermarket in 2025. Martin Dole, the commissioner of NT police, stated that a lack of evidence prevented prosecution after a thorough investigation.  Marion Scrymgour, federal MP for Lingiari, and Lidia Thorpe, an independent senator and member of the Gunnai, Gunditjmara and Djab Wurrung people, expressed their disappointment and called for accountability and justice. The family of White has been provided with support by NT police as they mourn his death.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Death of an Indigenous man in police custody raises serious concerns about systemic issues.

articles.title: Wave of child abuse scandals shakes schools in Paris
articles.rephrased_article: A school assistant in Paris is facing trial for sexual mistreatment of young children, marking the latest case in a year-long scandal that has shaken the city's school system. City Hall, which employs the animateurs – non-teaching staff who care for children after school – faces criticism for its initial handling of complaints and inadequate recruitment practices.  The scandal has led to widespread distrust among parents, with many accusing City Hall of failing to take their concerns seriously. The mayor, Emmanuel Grégoire, has pledged reforms including increased training and monitoring, as well as automatic suspension of animateurs after a single complaint.

articles.title: Two men arrested in connection to Dezi Freeman’s movements after Porepunkah shootings | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police have arrested two men in connection with the months-long manhunt for Dezi Freeman, who killed two police officers in August. The arrests are part of Operation Summit, which investigates Freeman's movements after the shootings at Porepunkah.  The investigation is ongoing and no further details were provided by police.

articles.title: Drunken brawl turns deadly: Labourer beaten to death near construction site, accused arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Whitefield police have upgraded a suspected accidental death case to murder after discovering evidence of a fatal assault near an under-construction building in Kundalahalli.  The deceased, S. Mehboob Basha, 59, was found dead and the accused, Sundaramurthy alias Shankar, 26, has been arrested. He is being held for questioning under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

articles.title: CBI takes over probe in Twisha Sharma death case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CBI registered an FIR in the Twisha Sharma dowry death case on May 25, 2026, after taking over from the Bhopal Police. The Madhya Pradesh High Court granted two days to retired judge Giribala Singh to respond to challenges to her anticipatory bail.  The Bhopal Police SIT interrogated Ms. Singh and recreated events at her house where Twisha Sharma was found dead. A Supreme Court bench assured a fair, independent investigation of the case.

articles.title: Court allows police interrogation of Shiv Sena MLA Sanjay Gaikwad over threat to publisher - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kolhapur court has granted permission for police to question Shiv Sena MLA Sanjay Gaikwad in connection with threats made against publisher Prashant Ambi regarding the book "Who was Shivaji?".  Gaikwad, who had previously objected to the use of the word "Shivaji" in the book and threatened Ambi, now regrets his abusive language but maintains he will continue to oppose books critical of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The incident dates back to 1988 when the book was published, and Mr. Ambi has received threatening calls since then.  The case is expected to proceed with a notice issued by the Rajarampuri police station directing Gaikwad to appear for questioning or submit a written response.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by an elected official against a publisher is a serious concern.

articles.title: Bengaluru digital arrest scam: Accused linked to ₹15 crore Belagavi cyber fraud too - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Six inter-State cyber fraud suspects arrested in connection with a ₹24 crore "digital arrest" scam in Bengaluru have also been linked to another ₹15 crore case in Belagavi. Palak Bhai Patel and Amit Narendra Patel, from Ahmedabad, are accused of involvement in the Belagavi case, which was registered with the Cyber Crime Police Station (CCPS). The suspects are currently in custody of the Bengaluru City Cyber Crime Police for further investigation.  The police have recovered ₹1.46 crore so far, while another ₹1.40 crore is under recovery.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale cyber fraud is being reported as routine.

articles.title: Father sentenced to 20 years in prison in POCSO case in Ranga Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 37-year-old laborer from Kurvaguda village in Shabad mandal was sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment and a ₹7 lakh compensation for sexually assaulting his daughter. The Shabad police registered a POCSO case based on the victim's complaint filed on October 12, 2024.  The court found him guilty under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Sexual assault of a minor is a serious crime and should be treated as an urgent concern.

articles.title: Police launch cybercrime prevention training for constables in Vijayawada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S.V. Rajashekar Babu, the Police Commissioner of the commissionerate, launched a five-day training program called "NTR Police Khaki Studio" for police constables on Monday (May 25, 2026). The program aims to train one constable from each police station in cyber safety and prevention of cyber offences using Artificial Intelligence. Deputy Commissioners of Police Shareen Begum, K.G.V. Saritha, K. Krishna Prasanna, and B. Lakshmi Narayana, along with other officers, were present at the launch.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: SC pained by handling of case, asks media to exercise restraint; CBI team dispatched to Bhopal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court intervened in the death of former model-turned-actor Twisha Sharma, urging media to exercise restraint while reporting developments. The court expressed concern over the handling of the case and stated it would ensure a fair and impartial investigation.  Solicitor General Tushar Mehta argued that media intervention had led to significant progress in the case, highlighting the importance of parental responsibility. Sharma's family has alleged procedural lapses and evidence tampering, prompting the court's involvement.

articles.title: Seven arrested in attempted contract killing case in Periyapatna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Periyapatna have arrested seven individuals, including the complainant's uncle, Saude Raju, for their alleged involvement in an attempted contract killing. The suspects, who include Shafi, Meer Hussain Ali alias Sultan, and Nayaz Ahmed, allegedly conspired to murder Praveen Kumar.  The investigation revealed that Raju hired Shafi to kill his nephew for a ₹7 lakh sum, while Sultan was contracted for ₹30 lakh. The police seized various items including a machete, a car, and mobile phones during the operation.

articles.title: Madhu lynching case: Kerala HC enhances sentence of 12 accused to life imprisonment, acquits one - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court acquitted Husain, the first accused in the 2018 lynching of Madhu, a mentally challenged tribal youth. The court sentenced the other 12 accused to life imprisonment and fined each ₹2 lakh.  The court found that the prosecution failed due to community apathy and inadequate witness protection.  Madhu's mother, Malli, had sought enhanced punishment for the accused. The case highlighted the importance of electronic evidence in criminal justice, as three CCTV cameras, six mobile phones, a GPS chip, call detail records, and forensic analysis played crucial roles in revealing the truth.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Lynching of a vulnerable individual with inadequate justice highlights systemic failures.

articles.title: Czech police detain Russian priest over ‘white substance’ find | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Czech police detained a Russian Orthodox priest, Bishop Hilarion, after discovering four containers of a suspicious white substance in his car. Moscow condemned the detention as an "orchestrated provocation" and demanded his immediate release. The Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman called the incident unacceptable high-handedness by the Czech authorities.  Hilarion denied any involvement in drug possession and claimed he was not given clear reasons for the police stop.

articles.title: Thoothukudi schoolgirl sexual assault and murder case: Man gets death penalty on two counts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dharma Muneeswaran, 38, of Sayalkudi, was sentenced to death by a special court in Thoothukudi for the sexual assault and murder of a 17-year-old schoolgirl. The girl went missing on March 10th and her body was found murdered on March 11th near her residence.  The Kulathur police conducted an investigation and sent the body to the Thoothukudi Government Medical College and Hospital for post-mortem examination.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Sexual assault and murder of a minor is a grave crime demanding urgent attention.

articles.title: Three arrested after 30-year-old woman shot dead in Sheffield city centre | Sheffield | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Yorkshire police are investigating the death of a 30-year-old woman who was shot outside a bar in Sheffield city centre. The incident occurred early this morning at the One Four One bar on West Street, where she was found with serious injuries and later died at the hospital. Three people, including a 30-year-old man detained in Sheffield and two others intercepted near Stockport, have been arrested on suspicion of murder.  The investigation is ongoing and police are urging anyone who witnessed the incident to come forward.

articles.title: ‘Rape, murder’ of minor girl sparks outrage in Kashmir, one arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J&K Police arrested a local youth in connection with the alleged rape and murder of a 12-year-old girl in Budgam, central Kashmir. The victim's body was discovered several meters from her home on Sunday (May 24, 2026), along with a copy of the Quran and her shoes.  The incident sparked outrage, leading to calls for swift action from regional leaders and civil society groups. Peoples Democratic Party leader Iltija Mufti and National Conference leader Aga Syed Ruhullah expressed grief and demanded accountability. J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdulla condemned the murder and pledged government support for a thorough investigation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports the rape and murder of a minor, raising serious concerns about safety and justice.

articles.title: 'For Brothers': Major international gang busted in Canada, 17 Indians charged for extortion targeting South Asians - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Peel Regional Police announced the dismantling of a violent international extortion ring, "For Brothers," which targeted South Asian businesses and community members across Canada, the United States, and parts of California.  The CBSA arrested six individuals for immigration-related inadmissibility after their criminal cases are finished. The investigation began in December 2025 following reports of multiple business and residential attacks linked to the group.  Of those arrested, 17 men face charges related to 24 incidents, including arson and shootings involving 324 rounds discharged. Peel Regional Police chief Nishan Duraiappah stated that these arrests reflect a coordinated effort to disrupt these networks and hold those responsible accountable.

articles.title: Nasire Best had previous run-ins with Secret Service, court documents show
articles.rephrased_article: Nasire Best, who had prior run-ins with Secret Service agents, was fatally shot by officers after firing shots outside the White House.  Best previously obstructed a White House entry lane in June 2025 and told agents he was Jesus Christ, leading to a mental evaluation. He was arrested for unlawfully entering a federally controlled property but failed to appear for a hearing, resulting in a warrant for his arrest. President Donald Trump was unharmed during the incident.

articles.title: Sukhpreet Singh and Ramandeep Kaur accused of hiding newborn’s remains in Canada, mother found in critical condition - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Halifax Regional Police charged two relatives of the infant's mother with concealing the child's body and obstructing investigators after a newborn was found dead in wooded area near Halifax, Canada. The infant's remains were discovered on Sunday afternoon, prompting an investigation that began late Friday when hospital staff alerted police to a woman in critical condition who appeared to have recently given birth but without her baby.  The Nova Scotia Medical Examiner Service is expected to conduct an autopsy to determine the infant's identity and cause of death, while the woman remains hospitalized in critical condition.

articles.title: Assault on Youth Congress workers in Alappuzha: SIT says 'assault unlawful’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) concluded that the assault on Indian Youth Congress activists in Alappuzha by police officers, including those from former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan's security detail, was unlawful. The SIT recommended criminal charges against the involved officers and found procedural irregularities in the initial investigation. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala will review the report before forwarding it to the Home Secretary for further action.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Police assault on citizens is unlawful and points to potential abuse of power.

articles.title: Hyderabad advocate murder: Police questioning continues; family seeks swift arrests - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad police are investigating the death of advocate Khaja Moizuddin, who was allegedly struck by an SUV near Masab Tank.  They have questioned about 10 individuals as part of the investigation, but have not disclosed details regarding the vehicle or the custody status of the accused. The victim's son, Farhan, expressed confidence in the police and judiciary while also alleging preferential treatment for the accused and a political angle to the case. Police have yet to respond to these allegations.

articles.title: Newly married couple shot dead in Karachi’s Malir area: police - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A newly married couple was fatally shot in Karachi's Saudabad locality while returning from a local court. SSP Fida Hussain Janwari of Korangi Police said the assailants, identified as the woman’s relatives, opened fire on their car after chasing them. The couple, aged 26 and 20 respectively, died at the scene.  Police Surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed confirmed multiple gunshot wounds. This incident follows a string of similar cases in Karachi where couples have been killed for alleged “honour” reasons.

articles.title: At least 19 taken to hospital after 'strong smell' reported at Tokyo mall
articles.rephrased_article: At least 19 people were taken to the hospital after a strong smell was reported at the Ginza 6 shopping center in Tokyo. A man is believed to have sprayed an irritant spray at a cash machine, causing throat pain and itching for those nearby. Police are searching for the suspect while emergency responders provided medical attention and cleared the area.

articles.title: Bondi beach gunmen shot 11 people within 30 seconds of opening fire, royal commission hears | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: At the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion, evidence was presented about the December 14th attack on a Hanukkah celebration at Bondi Beach. Sajid Akram and his son Naveed Akram, opened fire from a footbridge, killing 10 people and injuring three police officers.  The commission heard that Community Security Group requested a static police presence but was denied by NSW Police. The Asio director general, Mike Burgess, stated that while funding for counter-terrorism had decreased in favor of foreign interference and espionage, the agency is adequately resourced to address the evolving security environment.

articles.title: Dezi Freeman yelled abuse at dying police officer during shooting, Victorian coroner hears | Porepunkah shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dezi Freeman, also known as Desmond Filby, yelled abuse at Victoria police officers during a shooting that killed two officers investigating an alleged child sexual assault.  The incident began on August 26th when officers executed a warrant at Freeman's converted bus in Porepunkah.  Freeman shot and killed Det Leading Sen Const Neal Thompson and Sen Const Vadim De Waart-Hottart, before being shot dead by police seven months later. The state coroner is holding directions hearings for the inquest into the deaths of the officers, with speculation surrounding Freeman's whereabouts after the shooting.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Police officers were killed in the line of duty, raising concerns about officer safety.

articles.title: Pune school principal shared NEET-related questions for money: CBI tells court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, principal of Seth Hiralal Saraf Prashala, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Intelligence (CBI) for allegedly sharing NEET-UG exam questions and content with students in exchange for money. The CBI claims she collaborated with botany teacher Manisha Mandhare to prepare handwritten notes containing these questions and shared them via WhatsApp and printouts.  The investigation revealed that Havaldar received ₹20,000 from one student and ₹25,000 from another. Following the cancellation of the NEET-UG exam on May 3rd due to alleged paper leak, a re-examination is scheduled for June 21st.

articles.title: Man held on charge of theft - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajan alias Natarajan, a 61-year-old Tamil Nadu native, has been arrested in connection with the theft of 45 sovereigns of gold ornaments from a house in Bekal.  The Bekal police recovered the stolen jewelry from a hideout on Netaji Road near Kannur railway station following a complaint filed by the homeowner.

articles.title: Pregnant woman murdered over ‘Atla Taddi’ dispute; husband, father-in-law arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Meghana, a pregnant woman, was found dead on February 9th in Eluru district. Her husband, N. Pradeep, allegedly smothered her to death with a pillow and attempted to conceal the cause of death as cardiac arrest.  Police arrested Pradeep and his father, Narasimha Rao, after forensic evidence confirmed asphyxiation. The couple is currently in judicial custody.

articles.title: Elderly woman allegedly robbed of gold worth ₹11.6 lakh in Muvattupuzha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Muvattupuzha police are investigating a robbery case where an elderly woman, Mariyamma Paily, was allegedly robbed of gold ornaments worth approximately ₹11.6 lakh. The incident occurred on Sunday (May 24, 2026) at her residence when an unidentified suspect entered her bedroom, locked her domestic help in the bathroom, and stole the jewelry she was wearing.  The case has been registered under charges including wrongful confinement, house-trespass, and robbery under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.title: Assam Rifles apprehend key accused in 2023 abduction-murder of two Meitei students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam Rifles apprehended Nokjaging Baite Kuki, a key member of the United Kuki National Army (UKNA), wanted for the alleged abduction and murder of two Meitei students in July 2023.  The accused was found with an AK rifle, pistols, and grenades, and has been handed over to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) which is probing the case. The arrest follows a series of protests sparked by the discovery of the students' bodies in September 2023.  Lt Jamkhogin Guite, another UKNA member, was apprehended earlier for his involvement in multiple violent incidents including attacks on government officials and civilians.

articles.title: ‘Would shoot her’: Luigi Mangione fangirl says she would kill her pharmacist mother if she became a healthcare executive - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lena Weissbrot, a self-described "Mangionista," sparked outrage after making inflammatory comments about her mother, Reina Natero, who works as an executive at CVS Health.  Weissbrot claimed she would kill her own mother if she became a healthcare executive like the slain Brian Thompson, UnitedHealthcare CEO. She also expressed hypothetical scenarios involving inheriting money from her mother and "redistributing" it to families harmed by her alleged actions, while further criticizing Thompson's children. Weissbrot has become known for supporting Luigi Mangione, accused of killing Thompson, in court hearings.

articles.title: I wasn’t allowed to see her body, mother of murdered girl alleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A grieving mother of a 10-year-old girl who was murdered and sexually assaulted near Coimbatore, alleged that her husband cremated the body without her consent. The woman claims she was given no opportunity to see her daughter's remains and demanded police action against her husband and relatives. Minister for Transport A. Vijay Tamilan Parthiban and Minister for Backward Classes Welfare V. Sampath Kumar visited the girl’s native place in Salem district and provided a relief assistance of ₹7 lakh to the family.

articles.title: Man held for chopping sandalwood tree in Tirupattur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Thangaraj, a 42-year-old man from Jamunamarathur village, was arrested by Tirupattur Taluk police for chopping a sandalwood tree on the bund of a temple tank in Puthagaram village. The incident occurred around 7 a.m., when several devotees witnessed the act and apprehended Thangaraj while his accomplices fled.  The Tirupattur Taluk police and forest officials inspected the scene, registering a case and launching an investigation to apprehend the remaining suspects.

articles.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor faces police investigation into ‘alleged inappropriate behaviour at Royal Ascot’ | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is under investigation by Thames Valley police for alleged inappropriate behavior at Royal Ascot in 2002, as well as sexual misconduct. The investigation, which began after the release of documents from the US Department of Justice detailing his relationship with disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein, also covers potential misconduct in public office and a claim of sexual assault in 2010. Mountbatten-Windsor denies all wrongdoing.  The police are seeking witnesses who may have information about any criminal offenses involving the former prince.

articles.title: Warrants for defendants skipping court in England and Wales up 50% since 2020 | UK criminal justice | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: English and Welsh criminal justice system
articles.rephrased_article: Channel 4’s Dispatches investigation revealed that almost 60,000 arrest warrants were issued in England and Wales for defendants who skipped court last year, a nearly 50% increase since 2020. The number of outstanding failure-to-appear warrants is over 30,000, meaning thousands of criminals could be on the run after being charged. Alex Chalk KC, former justice secretary, stated that this situation is "a horror show" due to delays in the criminal justice system caused by factors like the Covid pandemic and underfunding.  The investigation also highlighted cases of wanted criminals who have evaded capture despite warrants issued against them.

articles.title: Who was Kamran Aman? UK delivery driver stabbed to death in racist attack by teenagers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marcus Staniforth, 17, and a 16-year-old boy were sentenced to life in prison with minimum terms of 17 years and 15 years respectively for the racist murder of Kamran Aman, a 38-year-old grocery delivery driver. The attack occurred outside Aman's mother's home in Barry, Wales, after the victim was targeted by the teenagers who had been drinking alcohol and taking drugs.  The case has now been referred to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme for review.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: final rites to be held in Bhopal after second autopsy by AIIMS Delhi team - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Twisha Sharma, a model-turned-actor, will be cremated at Bhopal's Bhadbhada Vishram Ghat on Sunday (May 24, 2026) after a second postmortem examination by a team of doctors from AIIMS-Delhi. The family expressed deep grief and emotional trauma over the delay in performing the cremation, citing traditional Hindu rituals.  Samarth Singh, Sharma's husband, was arrested on Friday (May 22, 2026) for his alleged involvement in her death.

articles.title: SC upholds consecutive life terms in multiple murder cases - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan affirmed the Lahore High Court's decision to impose consecutive life sentences on Qaiser Abbas, convicted of murdering two women. The court rejected Abbas' argument that concurrent sentencing was appropriate due to a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).  Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, writing for the bench, stated that imposing concurrent sentences would diminish the gravity of each murder and create an "artificial equivalence" between taking one life and multiple lives. The court upheld the trial court's decision, finding no grounds to interfere with its findings.

articles.title: 25 terrorists killed in Bannu clash - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A fierce clash between police, a peace committee, and terrorists in Bannu district resulted in the deaths of at least 25 terrorists, two police officers, and two civilians.  Police sources confirmed that the operation was launched after receiving information about the presence of a large number of terrorists in the area. The Lakki Marwat police peace committee also arrived to support the Bannu police.  The operation led to the deaths of two key terrorist commanders, Zmari Noor and Abdullah.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Loss of life, including civilians, in a clash with police raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Irish gangland figure fails in Dublin byelection bid for seat in parliament | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gerry “the monk” Hutch, an Irish gangland figure, failed to secure a parliamentary seat in a Dublin byelection. Daniel Ennis of the Social Democrats won the contest with 12,050 first-preference votes, defeating other candidates including Janice Boylan from Sinn Féin and Janet Horner from the Green party.  The election was held to fill the vacancy left by Paschal Donohoe, who resigned as a finance minister for a World Bank position. The victory of Ennis and the Social Democrats marks a shift towards progressive politics, while Hutch's defeat is seen as a relief for establishment candidates.

articles.title: TikToker held in Faisalabad for using obscene language for female tourists in Naran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A TikToker from Faisalabad, Yousuf, was arrested for making a video of female tourists at lake Saif-ul-Muluk using obscene language. The Roshanwala Police registered a case against him after identifying the suspect and he later confessed to profiting from creating such videos. In another incident, a 16-year-old girl suffering from cancer was allegedly kidnapped, gang-raped, and filmed by three individuals including a father and son in Faisalabad. The Saddar Police arrested the accused father and son based on the victim's mother's complaint.

articles.title: Kurnool police trace missing persons using facial-recognition CCTV network, says SP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kurnool district police are utilizing facial recognition technology (FRS) in over 722 Matrix Smart Technology CCTV cameras to locate missing persons, track criminals, and recover stolen vehicles. The cameras, installed across the state under the Andhra Pradesh FiberNet services, are monitored from a control room in Amaravati and linked to all district control rooms and police stations.  The technology has successfully located missing individuals in Madanapalle and Tirupati, according to Superintendent of Police Vikrant Patil.

articles.title: UK judge’s decision not to jail boys for rape like a ‘rock in my face’, says victim, 16 | Hampshire | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two teenage boys, aged 15 at the time of the offenses, were sentenced to youth rehabilitation orders for raping two girls in separate incidents. The judge's decision not to jail them has been met with criticism from victims and their families who expressed frustration and shock. Jodie Mittell KC, representing the prosecution, detailed how the boys exploited the victims through manipulation and coercion. Donna Jones, Hampshire police and crime commissioner, also criticized the sentence, stating that a custodial sentence was warranted. The attorney general's office has received multiple requests to review the sentences under the "unduly lenient" scheme.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The lenient sentencing for rape normalizes sexual violence against young girls.

articles.title: Bengaluru school headmaster arrested under Pocso Act, after minor student found pregnant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandraiah, a 59-year-old headmaster of a government higher primary school in Bengaluru, has been arrested under the POCSO Act for allegedly impregnating a minor student. The case came to light after the girl's pregnancy was discovered and police registered an FIR on May 22, 2026.  The girl has been provided medical care and counselling support, while members of the Child Welfare Committee have temporarily relocated her to a government rehabilitation facility. A separate incident involved a minor student escaping an attempted sexual assault by a physical education teacher at a government school in Byatarayanapura. The accused teacher was suspended following a complaint filed by the family and authorities provided support to the student.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a school headmaster against a minor is a serious crime.

articles.title: Australia news live: Queensland police shot dead man north of Brisbane; gunshots heard near White House | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queensland police shot and killed an alleged domestic violence perpetrator who was armed with a firearm at a home north of Brisbane. The incident occurred after midnight on Sunday morning, following reports that the man was making threats. Police Ethical Standards Command, with oversight from the Crime and Corruption Commission, will investigate the shooting. Three people were transported to hospital in stable conditions, while paramedics assessed a patient in a life-threatening condition at the scene.

articles.title: llegal LPG refilling unit busted in Chirayinkeezhu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Acting on a tip-off, officials from the Thiruvananthapuram district supply office raided a godown in Chirayinkeezhu, Kerala. The raid uncovered illegal LPG refilling operations where cylinders were being transferred for resale at inflated prices in the black market.  261 LPG cylinders belonging to various oil companies were seized along with equipment used for the operation. Further investigation is underway and prosecution proceedings will be initiated under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

articles.title: Cab driver assaulted on KH Road - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On May 22nd, a gang of armed men assaulted a cab driver on Double Road in Wilson Garden Police Station limits. The incident was captured on CCTV and has since gone viral.  The police are investigating the motive behind the assault and examining footage from nearby areas to identify the attackers. They are also tracing the registration numbers of both the Uber cab and the vehicle used by the assailants.

articles.title: Police constable’s wife found dead; dowry harassment case registered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lakshmi Priya, a 26-year-old woman, was found dead at her home in Mysuru on Friday. Rajesh Aaradhya, Lakshmi's husband and a police constable, informed her family that she had died.  The police are investigating the incident and suspect it may have been related to an ongoing family dispute. The case is being investigated under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Dowry Prohibition Act.

articles.title: Supreme Court registers suo motu case over death of Twisha Sharma - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the alleged dowry death of Twisha Sharma, a Noida resident, after allegations by her family regarding procedural irregularities and tampering with evidence in the investigation.  A three-judge Bench will hear the case on May 25th. The Sharma family alleges mental harassment and financial demands from her husband, Samarth Singh, and his mother, prompting the family to seek scrutiny of phone records and other material connected to the case.  The Madhya Pradesh High Court ordered a second autopsy by an AIIMS Delhi team following demands by Sharma's parents.

articles.title: Cricket betting racket busted, four arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chilakalapudi police arrested four individuals in connection with an online betting operation on IPL cricket matches.  The suspects, P. Dharani Kumar, P. Ravi Kumar, Ch. Ravindra Kumar and I. Satyam, were apprehended during a raid at Edepalli on Friday night. The Krishna district SP, V. Vidyasagar Naidu, confirmed the seizure of ₹36,000 in cash and eight mobile phones from the suspects' possession.

articles.title: Driver held for illegal sand mining from Palar River in Tirupattur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Mariappan, a 42-year-old driver from Tirupattur, was arrested by Natrampalli police near Jolarpet town for illegal sand mining from the dry river bed of Palar on Saturday.  The police seized a tipper lorry carrying loads of river sand and registered a case after finding it during a patrol on Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48). The driver fled the scene before being apprehended using CCTV footage analysis. A probe is ongoing.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: husband Samarth Singh brought to Bhopal, police to seek remand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samarth Singh, the husband of Twisha Sharma, who was found dead in her marital home on May 12th, 2026, was arrested by Madhya Pradesh police after he surrendered at a Jabalpur district court.  He is being held for questioning regarding his alleged involvement in dowry death and harassment. The case has prompted the State government to recommend a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Sharma's death.  The investigation is ongoing, with Giribala Singh, former judge and chairperson of the Bhopal Consumer Court, stating she is willing to provide a statement but has not yet been contacted by police.

articles.title: Brampton man Gurkanwal Singh pleads guilty after shooting guns from jeep in 'careless and unsafe' stunt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 24-year-old Sikh man, Gurkanwal Singh, pleaded guilty to careless use of a firearm in Bracebridge court after videos showing him firing guns recklessly from a Jeep on Crown land in Ontario sparked an investigation. The incident occurred in February 2025 and involved the discovery of firearms inside the vehicle, with footage obtained from an Instagram account linked to Singh.  The case is expected to return to court later this month for sentencing.

articles.title: Tahsildar’s vehicle set on fire in Walajah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tahsildar's official vehicle was set on fire early Saturday morning at the taluk office in Walajah town, Ranipet.  Firefighters extinguished the blaze before it spread further, but the vehicle was severely damaged. Security personnel observed a masked individual setting the SUV ablaze inside the premises and fled the scene. Police are investigating the incident and analyzing CCTV footage to identify the suspect.

articles.title: Man held for stone pelting near Arani - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Government Railway Police (GRP) arrested a 34-year-old man, T. Joseph Mani, for damaging the glass windows of the Howrah express train near Arani town in Tiruvannamalai after an argument with other passengers.  Mani pulled the emergency chain to stop the train and threw stones at the windows before being apprehended by railway police. An investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: ‘Clever and street-smart’: Police say Anmol did not employ anyone permanently - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anmol, an alleged cocaine queenpin arrested in Karachi, operated a sophisticated drug network across Pakistan. She began her illicit activities after separating from her husband, Rana Nasir, who was also an alleged drug dealer.  She hired several associates to supply drugs and launder money through various methods, including using a network of 35 riders, a police officer, and foreign contacts. Police have seized properties and frozen bank accounts linked to Anmol, while investigations continue with the Punjab Police, NCCIA, FIA, ANF, and Nadra.

articles.title: Three dead and 18 first responders sickened by apparent fentanyl exposure in New Mexico | New Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Three people died and 18 first responders were hospitalized in New Mexico after exposure to fentanyl at a rural home.  The Mountainair police department responded to reports of unresponsive individuals, finding four unconscious residents. Preliminary findings suggest the deaths were caused by fentanyl and methamphetamine. The cause of the incident is still under investigation, but authorities believe it was not a manufacturing site. Steve McLaughlin, chief medical officer at the University of New Mexico hospital, stated that fentanyl's potency makes even small amounts dangerous.  Matt Broom, the New Mexico state police chief, emphasized the need to address the opioid epidemic and protect first responders from exposure.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma’s husband sent to 7-day police remand; AIIMS Delhi forms panel for second autopsy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samarth Singh, husband of actor-model Twisha Sharma, was sent to seven days of police custody in Bhopal following his arrest for dowry death and harassment. AIIMS Delhi formed a four-member panel to perform a second autopsy on Sharma's body after the Madhya Pradesh High Court ordered it.  The probe team is investigating Mr. Singh's alleged role in Sharma's death, including questioning him and his mother, Giribala Singh, who was also named as an accused. The family has demanded a CBI investigation into the case, alleging police misconduct and influence from the accused family.

articles.title: Balochistan CTD kills 4 alleged terrorists in Pishin operation - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Balochistan Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) conducted an operation in the Surkhab refugee camp area of Pishin district, resulting in the deaths of four suspected terrorists. The CTD recovered a significant amount of weapons and explosives from their hideout.  The bodies were taken to the Quetta Civil Hospital for identification. This follows a series of operations targeting terrorism in Balochistan, including the killing of the mastermind behind the September 2025 suicide attack on the FC headquarters and the deaths of numerous suspected militants over the past year.

articles.title: Indian-origin cancer specialist banned from practising in UK says, 'I will never work in that country again' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shamir Chandran, an Indian-origin oncologist, has been struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal ruled that his criminal conviction made him a risk to the public.  The Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) found Chandran guilty of controlling and coercive behaviour and cruelty to a person under 16, and he fled the UK before the proceedings. The tribunal deemed allowing Chandran to continue practicing medicine would damage public trust in the profession.

articles.title: Indian national arrested after $5.6 million meth-making chemical found hidden in food consignment at Sydney port - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Australian Border Force (ABF) officers seized approximately 166kg of pseudoephedrine, a controlled chemical used in methamphetamine production, from an Indian-origin shipment at Sydney's Port Botany. The man who attempted to collect the consignment was charged with importing a border-controlled precursor under section 307.11(3) of the Criminal Code (Cth). ABF Superintendent Shaun Baker highlighted the effectiveness of intelligence-driven operations in preventing drug trafficking.

articles.title: Coimbatore girl's murder: police arrested two persons - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Inspector General of Police (West Zone) R.V. Ramya Bharathi announced the arrest of K. Karthi and R. Mohan, both residents of Pallapalayam near Coimbatore, in connection with the sexual assault-cum-murder of a 10-year-old girl found near Kannampalayam tank on Friday (May 22, 2026).  The duo confessed to luring the child, sexually assaulting her, and subsequently murdering her in a nearby coconut grove. They were remanded in judicial custody until June 5 and May 27 respectively. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay expressed shock at the incident and instructed police to conduct a swift investigation. The case has sparked protests from residents demanding justice for the victim.

articles.title: French pair held until trial after boys abandoned by road in Portugal
articles.rephrased_article: Marine R and Marc B, a French woman and her partner, were ordered into pre-trial detention in Portugal after being accused of abandoning their two young boys on a roadside. The children, aged four and five, were found crying near Alcacer do Sal and are currently with a French foster family in Lisbon. Authorities believe the couple had no known connection to Portugal and are investigating their backgrounds further.  The case has garnered attention due to R's work as a sexologist and B's former career as a French gendarmerie officer.

articles.title: Fraudster trying to sell fake ancient statues to Sotheby’s foiled over bogus invoices | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Crowley, 46, was sentenced to a two-year suspended sentence for attempting to defraud Sotheby’s by selling fake ancient statues.  Crowley presented forged invoices claiming the statues were from 1976 and used printing methods that were 25 years too modern. Forensic analysis revealed the documents were fabricated, and the judge acknowledged Crowley did not intend to deceive but instead believed he inherited the items legitimately. Sotheby’s experts identified inconsistencies in the paperwork early on, preventing a potential fraud.

articles.title: London stabbing: Five men rushed to hospital after violent altercation, one arrested - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Five men were injured in a stabbing incident on Horn Lane in Acton, London, after a violent altercation.  Metropolitan Police responded to reports of multiple men being assaulted and stabbed at around 2:47 pm, with all five victims taken to the hospital. A suspect, aged 26, was arrested for grievous bodily harm (GBH) and drug possession. London Ambulance Service dispatched multiple emergency teams to the scene.  Police are investigating the incident and have increased security in the area.

articles.title: Delhi Police files supplementary chargesheet in Parliament breach case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Police Special Cell filed a nearly 14,000-page supplementary chargesheet against the accused in the 2023 Parliament security breach case. The chargesheet, submitted before the Patiala House Court, includes allegations of terrorist acts, criminal conspiracy, and provocation to cause riots under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).  The prosecution argued that the filing was appropriate given ongoing proceedings on framing of charges, while defense counsel objected, arguing it was an abuse of process. The court directed a hard copy be supplied to the defense counsel and listed the matter for further scrutiny on May 29th.

articles.title: ‘I will kill you Jews’: Man jailed for 5 years in UK over antisemitic threats near London synagogue - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A London court sentenced Tavius Jean-Charles, a 36-year-old man, to five years in prison for seven racially aggravated public order offences and one count of racially aggravated criminal damage.  Jean-Charles targeted six Jewish victims in Stamford Hill between October 2025 and March 2026, including shouting death threats at synagogue manager Barry Bard and threatening another resident, Joel Scher. He was arrested after witnesses reported his repeated death threats near synagogues, and later made a statement about blowing up Jewish schools. The case highlights the rising concern over antisemitic attacks in the UK, with authorities pledging to address hate crimes more swiftly.

articles.title: U.P. STF busts SSC exam-rigging racket in Greater Noida; seven held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) arrested seven individuals in Greater Noida for their involvement in rigging Staff Selection Commission (SSC) online recruitment examinations. The accused allegedly used proxy servers and dummy candidates to manipulate the exams for constables in the CAPF, SSF, and riflemen in the Assam Rifles.  Pradeep Chauhan, a Muzaffarnagar resident who established the online examination center "Balaji Digital Zone," was identified as the alleged mastermind of the racket. The STF recovered ₹50 lakh in cash, electronic devices, and other evidence during the raid. The investigation is ongoing with four other members of the gang still at large.

articles.title: Sulur minor girl abduction and murder: Law and order a serious concern in T.N., says Udhayanidhi Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, leader of the Opposition, expressed concern over 30 major crimes within 12 days of the new government assuming office. These incidents include sexual violence, ganja smuggling, and the abduction and murder of a minor girl in Coimbatore. Stalin called for swift justice for the victim's family and urged the Chief Minister to prioritize law and order to prevent future incidents.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh woman killed by boyfriend after she refuses to accompany him - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ali Mohammad, 25, has been arrested for allegedly strangling his 21-year-old girlfriend, Reshma, inside her home in Uttar Pradesh's Shamli district. The incident occurred on Friday evening, with family members present.  Police say Ali Mohammad attacked Reshma after she refused to accompany him somewhere and both he and his associate, Aliyas, were apprehended at the scene. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and police are continuing their investigation.

articles.title: Three die in ‘horrific’ south Sydney vehicle crash after police welfare check | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A man died in a crash in Sydney after fleeing from police who had been called to carry out a welfare check. The crash involved a white Audi that rolled over a barrier and struck a blue Toyota sedan, killing the man, the driver of the Toyota, and a passenger.  Police believe the Audi was traveling at "considerable speed" when the crash occurred. Investigations are continuing into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

articles.title: Drugged, raped and filmed: German woman alleges years of horrific abuse by ex-partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A German woman, 59-year-old Claudia Wuttke, has accused her former partner of drugging and raping her over a period of 16 years, with the alleged crimes captured on video.  Police discovered the videos in June 2025 after finding them on a laptop. The German authorities dropped investigations into 65 of the 67 alleged cases due to statute of limitations laws, leaving only two remaining cases for prosecution. Wuttke expressed her disappointment at the lack of justice and called it "unacceptable" that most of the abuse would go unpunished.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma: Rival claims of murder and suicide set off media frenzy after Indian bride dies
articles.rephrased_article: A dowry death case in India has sparked a media frenzy after the death of 33-year-old model and actor Twisha Sharma.  Twisha's parents allege she was tortured by her husband, Samarth Singh, and his mother, retired judge Giribala Singh, over dowry demands and that she was murdered. The police have lodged a case against the Singhs and are investigating whether her death was murder or suicide. Giribala Singh denies the allegations, claiming Twisha had mental health issues and committed suicide.  The case has drawn attention to the issue of dowry deaths in India, where thousands of women are murdered annually for bringing insufficient dowries.

articles.title: NCCIA uncovers gang selling data of govt officials to foreign entities; four arrested - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested four individuals in South Punjab for selling sensitive personal data of government officers to foreign entities. The suspects, identified as Arshad Tariq, Arham Bari, Anam Sabir and Mohammad Rizwan, were allegedly sharing the data with foreign intelligence agencies.  The NCCIA is investigating how the information was accessed and has directed government institutions to strengthen data security.

articles.title: Actor Momina Iqbal seeks FIR against PML-N MPA over alleged blackmail and harassment - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Momina Iqbal, an actor and model, filed a first information report (FIR) against PML-N MPA Saqib Chadhar for blackmail, harassment, and death threats.  Iqbal alleged that Chadhar began threatening her after she refused his marriage proposal, claiming he was already married to two women. She also provided evidence of the threats through WhatsApp messages and video calls. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz warned against any political pressure or attempts to exploit the situation for personal gain, stating the matter will be addressed strictly according to law.

articles.title: ACB books Medchal deputy collector in disproportionate assets case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) officials conducted searches on Marri Vamshi Mohan, a Special Grade Deputy Collector, and his associates following allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income. The searches uncovered properties valued at around ₹6.22 crore, including land plots, houses, and vehicles, along with cash and gold ornaments. Vamshi Mohan was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.  The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Tennessee execution called off after failed lethal injection
articles.rephrased_article: A Tennessee execution of Tony Carruthers, convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed after staff were unable to find a suitable vein for the lethal injection.  The Department of Corrections stated that while they found a primary IV line, they could not establish a backup line as required by protocol. Governor Bill Lee granted Carruthers a temporary reprieve from execution for one year. The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and other advocates have raised concerns about the trial's integrity and called for DNA testing. Kim Kardashian also joined the cause, urging supporters to demand the evidence be tested before it's too late.

articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for gold scam in US, picked 16 gold bars from elderly victims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Syed M Makki, a 38-year-old Indian man, was sentenced to 15.5 years in prison for his role in a gold scam targeting elderly victims across the US.  The scheme involved malware that tricked victims into believing they were dealing with legitimate authorities, leading them to liquidate their savings and purchase gold bullion. Makki acted as a courier, collecting gold bars from victims and delivering them to co-conspirators. The Justice Department reported that the scam resulted in over $4.75 million in losses for victims.

articles.title: Anmol alias Pinky sent to jail on judicial remand in narcotics, murder cases - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anmol, also known as Pinky, an alleged drug queenpin, was sent to jail on a 14-day judicial remand in multiple narcotics cases and a murder case.  She had already been booked in over a dozen criminal cases prior to her arrest earlier this month. Karachi police sought the Sindh government's permission to dispatch a team to Punjab to arrest Anmol’s brothers, ex-husbands, and other co-suspects involved in the drug trafficking network. A Lahore court allowed an FIR against Rana Muhammad Akram, Anmol’s former husband, who allegedly conducted an illegal raid on Yasmeen Tabassam's house.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh government proposes to transfer case to CBI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh government proposed transferring the dowry death case of Twisha Sharma to the CBI. The notification, issued by Home Department Secretary Krishnaveni Desavatu, cites the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act for extending investigative powers to the state.  The case, registered at Katara Hills Police Station, involves allegations of harassment and dowry-related deaths against her husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh.

articles.title: Gujarat Police trace 701 missing persons under ‘Operation Milap’ in two weeks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gujarat Police have successfully reunited 701 missing persons with their families through a statewide operation called Operation Milap, which ran from May 7 to May 21.  The initiative, aimed at reviewing pending missing person cases, involved analyzing old records and conducting fresh field verifications.
