The drive also included checking digital records, social media activity, transport locations, and shelter homes, with officials noting some cases were linked to trafficking networks. Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi stated the government provided resources for the operation.

articles.title: Over 2,000 gather in San Diego to mourn three men killed in mosque attack | Gun Violence News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Over 2,000 people gathered in San Diego to mourn the three men killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego. Amin Abdullah, Mansour Kaziha, and Nader Awad were remembered as heroes who delayed and distracted the teenage suspects during the attack on Monday.  The victims' bodies were laid to rest together later that day, with police considering the incident a hate crime. The shooting is currently under investigation.

articles.title: Fake call centres duping U.S. citizens busted in Bengaluru, man from Delhi, another from U.P. arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka State Cyber Command officials raided four fake call centers in Bengaluru, uncovering a sophisticated operation that defrauded U.S. citizens by impersonating a prominent American accounting firm. The accused, Prashanth and Akash, allegedly collected millions of rupees from victims through fake tax advice, license renewal services, and counterfeit software keys.  The investigation revealed the use of shell companies to launder money and a network of over 120 employees trained to deceive victims using US accents. Pronab Mohanty, Director General of Cyber Command, stated that further investigations will focus on tracing the money trail and identifying bank accounts used in the fraud.

articles.title: Calcutta HC orders setting up SIT of CBI to probe hushing up charges in R G Kar rape-murder case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ordered the creation of a three-member special investigation team (SIT) from the CBI to investigate the death of a trainee doctor at the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The court's decision follows allegations that evidence was destroyed and attempts were made to downplay the incident. The SIT will focus on the events leading up to the victim's cremation, including potential lapses in the initial investigation by both police and hospital authorities.  The team is expected to file a comprehensive report by June 25th.

articles.title: Assistant Director of Mines in Ranipet relieved of duties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Mohan, Director of Geology and Mining, relieved E. Srinivasarao, Assistant Director of the Ranipet office, of his duties due to allegations that he demanded ₹2 lakh in cash from a stone quarry operator to relax mining norms. The incident was reported to the Ministry of Natural Resources, Minerals and Mines, headed by Minister T.K. Prabhu.  A. Arumuganainar, Regional Joint Director of Geology and Mining (Villupuram), will now hold full additional charge of the post of AD of Geology and Mining for Ranipet district.

articles.title: Tennessee governor orders stay of execution after doctor can’t find vein | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Bill Lee of Tennessee granted a one-year stay of execution for Tony Carruthers, who was scheduled to be executed on Thursday.  Carruthers's lawyers argued that he is mentally incompetent and there was a lack of physical evidence linking him to the 1994 murders. The reprieve came after Carruthers's legal team filed a last-minute appeal citing difficulties locating his vein during the lethal injection attempt, as well as concerns about the physician contracted by Tennessee’s department of corrections.  Carruthers's case has drawn attention due to ongoing questions about his conviction and mental competency, as well as protests against his execution.

articles.title: Boys convicted of rape get non-custodial sentences as judge says they should not be criminalised unnecessarily | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Three teenage boys, aged 13 to 14 at the time of their crimes, were sentenced to youth rehabilitation orders ranging from 18 months to three years for their roles in a series of knife-point rapes and sexual assaults against two teenage girls. Judge Nicholas Rowland stated he wanted to support the boys' reintegration into society and avoid criminalising them unnecessarily due to their young age, low intelligence, and limited understanding of consent.  The judge acknowledged the seriousness of the crimes but emphasized that they were "very young" and had not been in any big trouble before. Donna Jones, Hampshire’s police and crime commissioner, expressed concern over the lenient sentences, stating they offer little comfort to the victims.

articles.title: At least 16 people killed in two attacks in northern Honduras | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: At least 16 people were killed in two separate incidents of gun violence in northern Honduras.  Edgardo Barahona, spokesperson for Honduras’s National Police, reported that at least 10 workers were shot dead on a palm farm in Rigores, while six officers from the Anti-Maras, Gangs and Organised Crime Police Directorate (DIPAMPCO) were killed during an anti-gang operation in Omoa.  Hector Benjamin Valerio Ardon, head of Honduras’s Joint Staff of the Armed Forces, pledged to find those responsible for the attacks. The incidents have prompted the National Police to issue a statement promising immediate action to capture suspects and protect vulnerable communities.

articles.title: Who is Mohammed Omar, $90-million fraud suspect in Minnesota, who jumped from balcony to evade FBI arrest? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammed Omar, charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and four counts of health care fraud, jumped from a fourth-floor balcony during an FBI arrest attempt in Minnesota on Thursday. Colin McDonald, Assistant Attorney General for the National Fraud Enforcement Division, urged the public to help capture Omar, who allegedly operated two companies, North Home Health Care and South Home Health Care, with Ibrahim Bashir Abdi to defraud the government of $90 million through falsified service hours. The scheme involved using disabled individuals as "lottery tickets" to generate millions of dollars for luxury purchases.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder: Judge orders ChudTheBuilder to wear GPS monitor and restrict social media use if released on bond - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, faces strict new bond conditions after a judge ruled on his possible release from custody. The restrictions, imposed due to serious charges including attempted criminal homicide and firearm offenses, include GPS monitoring, weapon surrender, social media bans, and limited communication.  If released on bond, Eatherly will be closely monitored and must strictly adhere to all court orders.

articles.title: Who is Maurice Shelmon aka Ant Jefe? No Jumper YouTuber and podcaster faces felony murder charge after LAPD arrest - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Maurice Shelmon, better known online as Ant Jefe, was arrested by the Los Angeles Police Department on May 19 in connection with a felony murder case.  Shelmon, a popular podcasting and YouTube personality, had built a large following through his music releases, reaction videos, and appearances on the No Jumper podcast. The arrest has surprised many of his followers, who expressed shock and disbelief during a livestream hosted by No Jumper hosts.

articles.title: Chennithala seeks report on parole granted to Periye murder convicts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following protests from the families of the victims in the Periye twin murder case, Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has requested a report on the parole granted to five convicts. The parole order was issued during the final phase of the previous Left Democratic Front government's tenure and the jail authorities clarified that prisoners are generally not allowed to leave during elections.  The family members of the victims plan to meet the Chief Minister and the Home Minister to file a formal complaint against the mass parole granted to the convicts.

articles.title: California hit-and-run: Indian man arrested by ICE after state releases him, 4-year-old victim expected to survive - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aman Kumar, an Indian man, was arrested by ICE after being released from jail in California on charges of felony hit-and-run following a traffic accident that injured a four-year-old boy.  The incident occurred in April 2026 when Kumar ran over the child while attempting to avoid traffic. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) accused California sanctuary politicians of releasing Kumar from jail despite his illegal entry into the US in 2023.

articles.title: Ecuador’s Disappeared | Crime | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ecuadorian authorities are under scrutiny for the disappearance of at least 50 people detained by security forces since 2024, as investigations into forced disappearances conducted by the military during a drug war intensify.  The Ecuadorian government's crackdown on drug cartels has resulted in record killings and heightened concerns about human rights violations. The film "Disappeared Fault Lines" investigates these cases, including the disappearance of Jonathan Villon, a father of three taken by soldiers in broad daylight in December 2024, and the deaths of four boys known as the “Malvinas 4.

articles.title: 5 Indians, 2 US businessmen: Inside India's call center operation that FBI shut down for fraud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The FBI shut down a call center operation in India that defrauded hundreds of elderly victims across the US and elsewhere. Adam Young and Harrison Gevirtz, two former CEOs of a telecommunications company, Ringba, pleaded guilty to misprision of a felony for their role in enabling the scam. The investigation revealed that Indian citizens Sahil Narang, Chirag Sachdeva, Abrar Anjum, Manish Kumar, and Jagmeet Singh Virk were convicted of similar charges. The FBI is urging consumers to be aware of tech support scams and report any suspicious activity.

articles.title: UK grooming case: 20 jailed for 277 years over rape and abuse of girls between 1995 and 2003 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty individuals have been sentenced to a combined 277 years in prison for their roles in a child sexual abuse investigation spanning from 1995 to 2003. Sajid Majid, Manaf Hussain, and Tariq Azam received the longest sentences, with Majid receiving 28 years for five counts of rape and three counts of indecent assault.  The Kirklees District Police described the investigation as exposing "truly appalling sexual abuse" carried out by "a large number of sexual predators." Detective Chief Inspector Rob Stevens praised the victims' courage in enduring lengthy trials.

articles.title: Indian-origin truck driver Shamsher Singh jailed for 6 years for raping woman he met on dating app in New Zealand - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shamsher Singh, a 33-year-old Indian-origin man, was sentenced to six years and nine months in prison for raping a woman he met on a dating app during a late-night freight run. Singh assaulted the victim inside his commercial truck while parked on a remote stretch of highway between Nelson and Blenheim in January 2024. The victim accepted an invitation from Singh to accompany him on a delivery after connecting online and meeting for lunch in Nelson.  The assault occurred during the return leg of the journey, with the victim being asleep inside the vehicle when Singh attacked her.  Judge Harrop noted that Singh ignored the victim's distress and showed no remorse, resulting in the full sentence.

articles.title: US lawyers say man on death row could be executed with expired lethal drugs | Death Penalty News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tennessee lawyers for Tony Carruthers are concerned the state may use expired lethal injection drugs during his execution on Thursday.  They argue that TDOC's response to their inquiries about drug expiration dates is insufficient and raises concerns about the safety of the execution process. The issue of expired drugs in executions has plagued several states, including Arkansas, Idaho, and Texas, leading to delays or even stops in executions.

articles.title: Police officer catches baby thrown from window of house on fire
articles.rephrased_article: A police officer in Kalamazoo, Michigan, rescued a baby from a burning home after the mother threw the infant from a window.  The officer spotted the mother through an upstairs window and instructed her to drop the baby to him. Both the mother and baby were transported to a hospital for evaluation but neither sustained injuries. The cause of the fire is still under investigation by the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety.

articles.title: Man charged with stealing camera equipment from Bondi shooting victim in aftermath of terror attack | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW police have charged a 35-year-old man with larceny and disposing of stolen property in connection to the Bondi Beach terror attack. The man allegedly stole camera equipment from one of the victims, a retired police officer and photographer, after the December 14th shooting that killed 15 people. During an investigation into the attack, detectives identified the theft and executed a search warrant in Sydney's north-western suburbs where they found stolen property, including a camera, handcuffs, electronic devices, and white crystal powder. The man was granted strict conditional bail to appear before Blacktown local court on June 22nd.

articles.title: SC issues notices to accused in Rawalpindi honour killing case after jirga rejects woman’s marriage choice - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan issued notices to the accused in an honor killing case involving a young woman from Rawalpindi who was murdered after a jirga rejected her choice of marriage. The case stems from an FIR filed by Zia-ur Rehman, alleging his wife's elopement with another man and subsequent murder at the behest of a jirga. Zafarullah and Rafaqat Mehmood, members of the jirga who were granted bail by the Lahore High Court, are among those facing charges. The Punjab Prosecution Department appealed against the high court's decision, arguing that the accused were fully involved in the crime and posed a threat to witnesses. The case was adjourned until June.

articles.title: Man arrested for murdering woman, dumping body in Tirupalya lake in Anekal taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ratan Das, a man from Assam, was arrested in connection with the murder of a 47-year-old woman whose body was found floating in Tirupalya Lake in Anekal taluk.  Police confirmed that the woman had been strangled and suffocated before being disposed of in thick grass near the lake. The investigation revealed that Das had an illicit relationship with the victim and confessed to killing her after pressure to marry. He is currently under judicial custody.

articles.title: Bannu police kill five militants after launching operation in district - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bannu Police have killed a highly wanted commander, Hiyatullah, and his accomplice during an operation targeting militants involved in the suicide attack on the Fateh Khel police post.  The police claim to have eliminated five terrorists within the last 24 hours following the attack which resulted in the deaths of at least 15 police personnel. The operations were conducted under the special directives of RPO Sajjad Khan and involved intelligence-based operations (IBOs) and specialized police teams. Civil society and local residents praised the Bannu Police for their commitment to maintaining law and order, while the Police Peace Committee launched an operation titled “Operation Revenge of the Martyrs” with a focus on reclaiming militant hideouts and holding individuals linked to them accountable.

articles.title: Alleged drug queenpin Anmol remanded into police custody till May 22 in narcotics case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate in Karachi remanded alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky into police custody until May 22nd.  She was arrested earlier this week for possession of narcotics and an unlicensed weapon, and is already facing multiple criminal charges. The police sought her physical custody in a total of 15 cases but were denied in most instances, with some being sent to judicial remand. Anmol claimed she was tortured during custody and that the police are trying to harass her in court.  The investigation into her alleged drug network is ongoing.

articles.title: Two men arrested in London after man run over by van in Birmingham | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two men were arrested in London after arriving for a protest in the capital. The arrests are related to an incident in Birmingham where a man was run over by a van on Thursday evening. West Midlands police are investigating the incident, which left a man in his 30s with a broken leg that required surgery.  The van involved in the incident has been recovered and is being examined.

articles.title: Cyberabad police begin search for Bandi Bageerath in Hyderabad and Karimnagar after HC rejects pre-arrest bail plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad police intensified their search for Bandi Bageerath, accused of sexually assaulting and emotionally manipulating a 17-year-old girl, by conducting searches at his residences in Hyderabad and Karimnagar.  Five police teams were involved in the operation, which included physical checks and surveillance efforts to track his whereabouts. The investigation is ongoing, with discussions about Bageerath surrendering to authorities before being subjected to medical examination and remanded.

articles.title: CBI arrests ‘mastermind’ linked to NEET-UG 2026 biology paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested a biology lecturer, Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, for her involvement in the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak case.  Mandhare, appointed by the National Testing Agency (NTA) as an expert, allegedly disclosed questions and answers from botany and zoology subjects to students through special coaching classes at her residence. The agency has arrested nine individuals in connection with the case, including a chemistry lecturer, P.V. Kulkarni, who allegedly leaked chemistry questions.  The CBI is conducting searches across the country and investigating leads related to the distribution of a "guess" paper that closely matched the actual exam paper.

articles.title: At least five people pardoned by Trump for Capitol attack accused of new crimes | US Capitol attack | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ryan Nichols, a former Capitol rioter pardoned by Donald Trump in January 2025, was arrested on May 11th in Texas for brandishing a handgun during a dispute.  Nichols had previously pleaded guilty to his role in the January 6th insurrection and received a prison sentence. He later announced his withdrawal from a congressional race after facing new criminal charges. Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) has documented over 30 individuals pardoned by Trump who are now accused of committing crimes after their pardons.

articles.title: Adhikari aide killing: CBI conducts searches at multiple locations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The CBI conducted searches at multiple locations in connection with the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandrakant Rath. The agency took over the investigation from the West Bengal Police, forming a seven-member special investigation team under a DIG of Special Crime from Delhi.  Rath was shot dead on May 6th, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the case, while police believe at least eight people were involved.

articles.title: Bahawalpur police look for suspect linked to ‘cocaine queen’ network - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bahawalpur district and regional police are investigating Tahir Saleem, a drug trafficker allegedly linked to the cocaine trafficking ring run by Ms Anmol alias Pinki.  Police confirmed that Tahir Saleem is from Hasilpur, Bahawalpur district. He was previously arrested in Lahore for supplying narcotics to students and is suspected of working with Ms Anmol alias Pinki. The police are currently reviewing his criminal records. In a separate incident, the bodies of a mother and her three children were found axed to death in Fatehpur, Vehari district.  The husband of the deceased has been taken into custody for questioning.

articles.title: Teenager Isla Bell’s body was found in a Melbourne tip 18 months ago. Today friends and family demanded ‘justice’ | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Isla Bell, a 19-year-old whose body was found in a Melbourne tip, was remembered by friends and family at a vigil on Saturday. Justine Spokes, Bell's mother, expressed her grief and frustration with the legal system after prosecutors dropped manslaughter charges against the man accused of killing her daughter, Marat Ganiev.  Spokes called for changes to protect vulnerable women and girls and emphasized the need for an end to "toxic masculinity" and violence against women. The vigil also saw calls for justice from Bell's family and community members who demanded a trial for Ganiev.

articles.title: NIA chargesheets ‘mastermind,’ four others in Cambodia-linked ‘cyber slavery’ case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) filed a charge sheet against five individuals, including absconding mastermind Anand Kumar Singh, in a case of human trafficking and “cyber slavery” in Cambodia. Three accused, Abhay Nath Dubey, Rohit Yadav, and Abhiranjan Kumar, were arrested upon arrival in Delhi from Cambodia in February. The syndicate lured Indian youth to Cambodia under false pretenses for legitimate jobs and lucrative salaries. Victims were forced to work for scam companies, subjected to mental and physical torture, including electric shocks, forceful confinement, and denial of food and water.  The NIA is working to track down the remaining members of the syndicate.

articles.title: Take strict action against officers making accused wear only undergarments in lockups: Kerala State Human Rights Commission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Human Rights Commission chairperson Alexander Thomas has called for strict action against police officers who make accused wear only undergarments in lockups. The commission issued the directive following a complaint filed by R.G. Leninraj alleging this practice violated human and fundamental rights. The ADGP (Law and Order) also reported that the police headquarters had instructed officers not to violate these rights, warning of disciplinary action for any violation.

articles.title: Man accused of killing two people outside Washington DC Jewish museum could face death penalty | Washington DC | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: US attorney for the District of Columbia
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department announced it will seek the death penalty for Elias Rodriguez, accused of fatally shooting two staff members of the Israeli embassy in Washington.  Rodriguez faces federal hate crime and murder charges for the killings of Yaron Lischinsky and Sarah Milgrim outside a Jewish museum last May. Prosecutors allege that Rodriguez was motivated by antisemitism when he opened fire on the couple, who were about to become engaged. The US attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, stated that anyone seeking political violence in Washington will face consequences.

articles.title: Elgar case: NIA seeks cancellation of bail of activists Sudha Bharadwaj and Varavara Rao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has requested a special court to cancel the bail of lawyer-activist Sudha Bharadwaj and poet-activist Varavara Rao, alleging they violated their bail conditions by attending a gathering at the Mumbai Press Club on January 19. The NIA presented evidence, including CCTV footage and call data records, suggesting the meeting was intended to propagate the ideology of the CPI (Maoist) and discuss the "Urban Naxal" movement.  The court has asked both individuals to respond to the agency's plea.

articles.title: Ex-Sinaloa security chief in Mexico arrested in US over alleged cartel ties | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gerardo Merida Sanchez, a former security chief in Mexico's Sinaloa state, was arrested in Arizona on May 11 and transferred to New York. He is accused of conspiring with leaders of the Sinaloa Cartel to import narcotics into the United States in exchange for political support and bribes.  Merida Sanchez allegedly accepted over $100,000 in monthly cash bribes from Los Chapitos, a powerful faction of the cartel led by the sons of jailed drug lord Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman. The indictment also accuses him of leaking sensitive intelligence to the cartel. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, has stated that she will not protect anyone who committed a crime but suggested the US charges were politically motivated.

articles.title: HC denies pre-arrest bail to Bandi Sanjay’s son, reserves order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court declined to grant pre-arrest bail to Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay's son, Sai Bageerath, in a POCSO Act case.  Justice T. Madhavi Devi reserved orders on the anticipatory bail petition and will pronounce them on May 21st. The judge heard arguments from both sides, with senior counsel S. Niranjan Reddy arguing that the relationship between the accused and the victim was amicable and the alleged offense might not be as severe as suggested in the FIR. Advocate Pappu Nageshwar Rao representing the victim's mother opposed the bail plea citing Supreme Court judgments rejecting anticipatory bails in POCSO cases and highlighting the trauma experienced by the victim. The Public Prosecutor for Home Palle Nageshwar Rao refuted the arguments of the petitioner’s counsel regarding an improvement in the FIR.

articles.title: Another mistrial declared in Harvey Weinstein rape retrial
articles.rephrased_article: Harvey Weinstein was declared guilty of rape in a New York trial, but the verdict was overturned. The judge declared a mistrial after the jury failed to reach a unanimous decision on whether he raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann in a hotel room over a decade ago. This is the third time a New York jury has considered this case against the 74-year-old disgraced film mogul, who remains jailed on other charges.

articles.title: AI vigilante trap snares alleged paedophile ex-teacher in France
articles.rephrased_article: A retired French sports teacher, Dominique B, was arrested in eastern France after engaging in a 40-minute online conversation with an AI-generated teenage girl. The video of the interaction, broadcast on several platforms and viewed by over 40,000 people, showed B making sexual propositions to the "girl," who was actually operated by influencer FINNYZYY.  The case has sparked debate about the ethics of entrapment methods used by FINNYZYY, a popular influencer who claims his aim is to raise awareness about child sex abuse.

articles.title: Indian-origin man convicted of attempted murder of woman and child in East London stabbing
articles.rephrased_article: Kulvinder Ram, a 48-year-old Indian-origin man, was found guilty of attempting to murder a woman and two children in east London last year. Ram also admitted to causing grievous bodily harm to another child during the attack.  The incident occurred in Dagenham in October 2024, leaving all three victims with serious injuries requiring surgery. An off-duty Metropolitan Police Special Constable, Seff Serroukh, intervened and restrained Ram until on-duty officers arrived. Detective Constable Lewis Whitlock stated that the investigation revealed Ram's intent to kill the victims.  Ram remains in custody awaiting sentencing.

articles.title: Yes, I did it: 22-year-old Indian pleads guilty to smuggling people across US-Canada border; $100 per head
articles.rephrased_article: A 22-year-old Indian man, Shivam, pleaded guilty to conspiring in a smuggling ring that transported Indians across the US-Canada border.  Shivam, who coordinated drivers and directed operations from October 2024 to June 2025, faces a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of fifteen years in prison. The operation was busted by US Border Patrol agents during a chase near the border on January 26, 2025.

articles.title: Boy, 15, shot dead in France as prosecutors blame drug war
articles.rephrased_article: French prosecutors believe a 15-year-old boy was killed and two other young men were injured in a suspected drug-related shooting in Nantes. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated the attack likely involved drug trafficking, but emphasized that the victims may have been innocent bystanders. The victim's aunt strongly denied any involvement with drugs, stating he was simply at the wrong place at the wrong time.  The city's mayor condemned the "drug trafficking plaguing the country" and called for increased police resources to find the attackers.

articles.title: Probe shows foreigners' involvement in network run by alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky: Karachi AIG - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan announced that investigations into Anmol alias Pinky, a drug trafficking suspect arrested in Karachi, are revealing potential transnational connections.  Khan stated that information suggests involvement of foreigners from African countries in Lahore and women in the network operating in Lahore. The AIG also revealed that Anmol has been involved in 20 cases across Sindh, with some dating back to previous years.

articles.title: Brutal raid on woman's birthday party highlights rise of Russian vigilante group
articles.rephrased_article: A vigilante group called Russkaya Obshina has been conducting raids across Russia, targeting individuals and businesses they deem to violate traditional values. The group, which is not officially registered but operates with police involvement, claims to uphold law and order while promoting traditional Russian culture and values.  The group's actions have led to the arrest of several individuals, including Katya, a woman who was raided during her birthday party for allegedly displaying a crucifix.  Russkaya Obshina has received funding from figures close to the Kremlin and has been linked to far-right groups in Ukraine. The group's activities are raising concerns about its potential impact on Russia's political landscape and human rights.

articles.title: Imam, 54, who claimed ‘jinn powers’ jailed for life over abuse crimes against women and girls
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Halim Khan, a former imam in East London, was sentenced to life imprisonment for 21 sexual offences against seven victims. The judge condemned his abuse of trust as "monstrous" and noted that he used supernatural claims to manipulate victims who were vulnerable due to their faith. Prosecutors highlighted the use of fear and isolation tactics by Khan to silence victims, allowing him to continue abusing them for nearly a decade.  The case has sparked national discussions about safeguarding failures within religious institutions and the challenges faced by victims coming forward.

articles.title: Punjab police want Anmol alias Pinky’s custody from Sindh - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab Police are seeking custody of drug dealer Anmol alias Pinky from Sindh Police after her arrest in Karachi for allegedly running a drug network.  The investigation has revealed that Anmol and her brothers, Nasir and Riaz Baloch, were involved in three drug cases registered in Lahore several years ago. The Punjab Police are also investigating allegations of bribery and negligence by former officers of the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) who allegedly avoided arresting Anmol.  The DIG investigation, Zeeshan Raza, stated that departmental action has been initiated against the officers involved.

articles.title: Death toll in explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas rises to five - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Five workers have died after an explosion at a firecracker factory in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, with 23 others hospitalized. Anil Malviya, the licensed owner of the factory, has been arrested under the National Security Act (NSA) and his license suspended.  Chief Minister Mohan Yadav visited the hospital where the injured are being treated, promising a thorough investigation into the incident. The state government is also conducting a magisterial inquiry and has ordered an investigation by officials from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), the State Pollution Control Board, and the Forensic Science Laboratory.

articles.title: 806 locals held, 97 properties attached, 41 demolished in anti-drug drive in J&K in 30 days: DGP Nalin Prabhat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The J&K Police conducted a major anti-drug campaign between April 11 and May 13, resulting in the arrest of 806 individuals under the NDPS Act, the attachment of 97 properties worth ₹41.85 crore, and the demolition of 41 properties linked to drug trafficking. Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat stated that these actions were part of a broader effort to dismantle drug networks operating across states and combat Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and narco-terrorism.  The campaign also saw the cancellation or suspension of driving licenses for 162 individuals involved in narcotics activities, the revocation of registration certificates for 92, and the impounding of 10 passports.

articles.title: Woman gang-raped inside bus in Delhi’s Rani Bagh, two arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Rani Bagh have arrested two bus drivers, Umesh Kumar and Ramender, for the gang-rape of a woman on a private sleeper bus. The assault occurred on May 11th after the woman refused to engage with the men following a monetary agreement.  The woman reported the incident to the police who seized the vehicle used in the crime. Both accused were apprehended within hours of the incident being reported and an FIR has been filed.

articles.title: ED arrests Kolkata Police DC Shantanu Sinha Biswas in money laundering case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials arrested Shantanu Sinha Biswas, Deputy Commissioner of Kolkata Police, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in land grabbing and money laundering linked to businessman Sona Pappu.  The arrest follows repeated summons by the ED and a lookout notice issued against him for failing to appear. The investigation is ongoing, with the ED seeking information from the West Bengal Police regarding Biswas' current deployment. This marks the second high-profile arrest by the ED since the change of regime in West Bengal.

articles.title: Brazilian influencer on the run after fleeing sentencing in fatal road crash case
articles.rephrased_article: Rosa Iberê Tavares Dantas, a Brazilian influencer, is now considered a fugitive after fleeing the country to avoid serving a three-year prison sentence for negligent homicide in a fatal road crash case. The 31-year-old personal trainer, Talis Roque da Silva, was killed when Dantas' SUV collided with his motorcycle in August 2023. Authorities have placed her name on Brazil’s National Register of Arrest Warrants and notified Interpol to assist in locating her.

articles.title: Constable injured in attack on checkpost succumbs to wounds in Charsadda - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Constable Sajjad Khan, who was critically injured in an attack on a checkpost in Charsadda, KP, last month, died from his wounds. The constable's funeral prayers were held with official honors at Police Lines Charsadda on Thursday, attended by the DPO, Superintendent of Police Investigation, and other officials.  DPO Mohammad Waqas Khan paid tribute to the slain constable's sacrifice, emphasizing the ongoing war against terrorism and the police force's role in maintaining peace.

articles.title: Streamer ChudTheBuilder charged with attempted murder after Tennessee courthouse shooting
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, has been charged with attempted murder after a shooting outside the Montgomery County courthouse in Clarksville on Wednesday.  Authorities confirmed that both Eatherly and another unidentified man were injured during an altercation, and are currently in stable condition. The incident has sparked renewed discussion about Eatherly’s controversial online behavior, which includes alleged racial slurs and provoking strangers during livestreams.  The Montgomery County Sheriff's Office is investigating the case.

articles.title: Trading in organs illegally in Kerala, with forged documents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A middle-aged man, dressed shabbily, visited the Superintendent of Police (Ernakulam Rural) in Aluva to obtain a police clearance certificate for an organ donation. He intended to donate one of his kidneys to a patient unrelated to him. The officer handling the application questioned him about how he met the recipient, which led to unexpected revelations.

articles.title: Hundreds of illegal motorbikes bulldozed in NYC crime crackdown
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Police Department (NYPD) bulldozed over 200 illegal motorbikes and scooters in Staten Island as part of a city-wide crackdown on unregistered vehicles.  This action follows a recent tragic incident where a 7-month-old was killed by a stray bullet from an illegal moped, prompting the NYPD to increase enforcement efforts. The NYPD has seized over 5,700 such vehicles since the beginning of 2026, marking a 10% increase compared to the same period in 2025.

articles.title: CBI arrests key accused in cyber fraud case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Lakhan Jaiprakash Jagwani, a key suspect in a transnational cyber-enabled financial fraud case involving illegal call centers targeting U.S. nationals. The syndicate operated since 2022 and impersonated officials from agencies like the DEA, FBI, and Social Security Administration to defraud victims of $8.5 million.  The agency previously seized ₹1.88 crore in cash from an "illegal" call center run by Jagwani in Noida.

articles.title: Paediatrician in Germany charged with 130 counts of sexual abuse | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: German prosecutors have charged a 46-year-old paediatrician with 130 counts of sexual abuse, including rape, committed between 2013 and 2025. The alleged crimes occurred at clinics operated by the Havelland healthcare group in Brandenburg state. The doctor is accused of abusing most of his patients while they were under his care.  The case has prompted investigations into safeguarding procedures at clinics across the region, with the Havelland Kliniken group pledging full support to prosecutors and providing any relevant information. A regional court will decide whether to proceed to trial.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his involvement in a large-scale securities fraud scheme. Parmar, also known as Paul Parmer, pleaded guilty in 2025 and orchestrated the scheme with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis (aka 'Sam Zaharis') and Ravi Chivukula. The conspirators defrauded a private investment firm and others out of hundreds of millions of dollars by inflating the value of a healthcare services company.  The scheme involved falsifying bank records, creating phony customers, and misrepresenting financial information to raise money for acquisitions that did not exist.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his role in a large-scale investment fraud scheme. Parmar, along with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors by inflating the value of a healthcare services company and securing funding through fraudulent means. The conspirators misrepresented the company's financial performance, causing victims to believe it was worth significantly more than its actual value.  The scheme ultimately led to the company's bankruptcy in 2018.

articles.title: Gwadar University VC, pro-vice chancellor 'go missing' while travelling to Quetta - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir and Syed Manzoor Ahmed, the vice chancellor and pro-vice chancellor of the University of Gwadar, have gone missing after leaving for Quetta on Wednesday. The pair, along with a driver and another university employee, were last seen near Mastung on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway.  Police officials suspect kidnapping as they haven't been in contact since reaching the Khud-Kocha area. Babar Yousafzai, an aide at the Balochistan Home Department, confirmed that efforts are underway to locate them.

articles.title: Saleh Mamman: Former Nigerian power minister sentenced to 75 years for corruption
articles.rephrased_article: Saleh Mamman, a former Nigerian power minister, was sentenced to 75 years in prison for laundering $24.7 million in public funds. Mamman, who led the ministry under President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2021, was found guilty of 12 counts related to using private firms to funnel money linked to government-funded power plants.  The case is part of a wider anti-corruption drive targeting former government officials in Nigeria. The high court ordered Mamman to repay $16 million and his conviction has reignited public anger over the country's chronic electricity crisis.

articles.title: Victorian Labor signals tougher stance on young offenders after 109 charges against 14-year-old dropped | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victorian Labor government officials stated they will "toughen consequences" for young offenders after 109 charges against a 14-year-old girl were dropped due to concerns regarding the doli incapax rule. The girl was accused of multiple offenses, including reckless conduct endangering serious injury and burglary, following a two-month crime spree earlier this year. Liberal MP David Southwick criticized the justice system's failure to hold the girl accountable for her actions, while Premier Jacinta Allan acknowledged the unacceptable behavior but did not comment on specific details of the case.

articles.title: Blaze erupts after explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas; casualties feared - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire and explosion at an alleged illegal firecracker factory in Dewas district, Madhya Pradesh, resulted in multiple casualties. Police and administration personnel launched rescue operations after the incident, which occurred in Tonk Kalan area.  Local residents reported the factory was producing illegal fireworks.

articles.title: Influencer detained in Tennessee over alleged confrontation involving gunfire | Tennessee | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as Chud the Builder, was detained in Tennessee following a shooting incident outside the Montgomery county courthouse.  Eatherly allegedly opened fire during a confrontation with another man, sustaining a gunshot wound to his arm and injuring the other individual who was transported by Lifeflight to Vanderbilt University Medical Center. The Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office praised their deputies for preventing further escalation of the situation. The District Attorney General's office is reviewing the facts of the investigation for formal criminal charges.

articles.title: Three held; security beefed up in Bhopal as Muslim community protests assault on man over ‘love jihad’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three men were arrested in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, following a protest by members of the Muslim community who demonstrated against an assault on a man by Bajrang Dal activists. The incident occurred after several videos of the assault, which allegedly involved derogatory language and insults to Islam, went viral online.  The Muslim community demanded that the accused be arrested within 24 hours.  Ayush Gupta, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Bhopal zone 1, confirmed searches for more suspects and stated that adequate security has been implemented in sensitive areas. Bittu Sharma, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Jahangirabad, reported increased police presence in these locations to maintain peace. The incident followed a previous attack on Arif Khan, a 27-year-old man from the Muslim community, by right-wing activists who accused him of "love jihad."

articles.title: Alien smuggling and child sexual abuse material: Iranian national pleads guilty in New York court to two serious federal crimes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Sharon Gohari, a naturalized US citizen of Iranian descent, pleaded guilty to charges of alien smuggling and receiving child sexual abuse material in federal court.  Gohari operated a scheme from at least December 2020 until May 2025, facilitating travel for Iranian nationals seeking entry into the US for thousands of dollars per client. Authorities discovered child sexual abuse material on Gohari's phone, including videos depicting the rape of children as young as five years old, and he shared some with overseas accounts in Iran.  Sentencing is scheduled for a later date.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of rape after woman alleges assault near church in Maidstone - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kent Police arrested a 50-year-old man on suspicion of rape following an alleged assault near a church in Maidstone. The incident occurred between 7 pm and 10 pm on Saturday, with the woman reporting the attack to police late that evening.  The suspect remains in custody while police continue their investigation, cordoning off the area and urging residents with CCTV or dashcams to check for footage.

articles.title: Valdo Calocane brother tells inquiry he felt powerless over killer’s mental ill health | Nottingham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, stabbed to death three people and injured others in Nottingham on June 13, 2023. His younger brother, Elias, testified at an inquiry into the events leading up to the attacks, stating he believed his brother's violent messages concerned suicidal thoughts.  Elias said he had a "belief" that Calocane would take his own life and saw him as having "darkest thoughts". The inquiry heard that Calocane had called his brother on the day before the attacks, asking him to take their parents out of the country.

articles.title: ATS questions 57 in Maharashtra over alleged gangster network links - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) officials conducted searches across several cities in the state as part of an operation targeting alleged networks linked to Pakistani gangsters, including the Shahzad Bhatti gang and the Dogra gang. The focus is on identifying sleeper cells, local operatives, and support systems that may facilitate arms smuggling or conspiracies.  ATS teams seized electronic devices and are examining bank accounts and financial transactions to determine if funds were routed from Pakistan through hawala channels.

articles.title: Two locals, including teacher, held for ‘providing logistic support’ to Saifullah terror group in Kishtwar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J&K Police arrested two locals, a school teacher and another individual, in the Chenab Valley's Kishtwar for allegedly aiding foreign terrorists. Mashkoor Ahmed, a teacher with the School Education Department, was directly implicated in facilitating the terrorists' hideout, while Maneer Ahmed is also accused of providing support to the Saifullah group. The police are continuing their investigation and have lodged an FIR under the Arms Act and UAPA against the suspects.

articles.title: Harshkumar Patel seeks to quash conviction in case linked to Indian family’s freezing deaths at US-Canada border - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harshkumar Patel, a man convicted in a human smuggling case linked to the deaths of an Indian family near the US-Canada border, has appealed his conviction and sentence. He claims legal errors impacted his trial, specifically regarding jury instructions and sentencing. Patel, who is now representing himself, seeks to vacate all convictions or overturn selected charges and resentencing. His co-accused, Steve Shand, also filed an appeal challenging his conviction and sentence, arguing that the traffic stop leading to his arrest was unlawful and that he was unaware of the smuggling operation's leader's decision to cross a family with young children in dangerous conditions.

articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang stakes claim on gunfire outside Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Karnal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema alleged that the Lawrence Bishnoi gang was responsible for an alleged firing incident outside the residence of Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Haryana.  Tyson Bishnoi, Arzoo Bishnoi, and Hari Boxer, purportedly acting on behalf of the Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the incident via social media. Cheema accused the BJP of using gangsters to intimidate Punjabis who refuse to join their party. The Haryana Police have not received a complaint from the manager or his family and found no evidence at the scene.

articles.title: Epstein abused me while under house arrest, survivor tells US lawmakers
articles.rephrased_article: A survivor of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse, Roza, testified before House Democrats in West Palm Beach, Florida, detailing how she was sexually abused while he was under house arrest.  Roza, who was recruited by Jean-Luc Brunel, Epstein's associate, said she was offered work to help with her financial troubles and that Epstein subjected her to rape over three years. The hearing, organized by Democratic lawmakers from the US House Oversight Committee, aimed to keep the Epstein case in the spotlight and highlight the failures of the justice system in holding him accountable.

articles.title: Man dies in Sydney prison unit that watchdog wanted shut down because it ‘cannot provide a safe environment’ | Prisons | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old man died by suicide at the Metropolitan Special Programs Centre (MSPC) in Long Bay correctional centre on Sunday.  The Corrective Service NSW is investigating, and any death in custody is subject to a public inquiry. The inspector for custodial services recommended the closure of three units at Long Bay, including the MSPC, due to concerns about safety and living conditions. The report cited run-down rooms, inadequate ventilation, and ligature points as contributing factors.  The Greens justice spokesperson, Sue Higginson, had previously called for the closure of the unit, citing risks to inmates' lives.

articles.title: Police register FIR after viral video shows BJP worker’s kin firing into the air at wedding - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Raipur, Chhattisgarh registered an FIR on Tuesday after a viral video showed individuals firing guns at a wedding function. The DD Nagar Police stated that the incident violated firearm license conditions and could be considered negligence under various laws, including the BNS and Arms Act.  The video sparked outrage online and backlash from the Opposition.

articles.title: South Carolina court tosses murder conviction in Alex Murdaugh case | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The South Carolina Supreme Court overturned the murder conviction of lawyer Alex Murdaugh, citing comments from a court clerk that unfairly influenced the jury. The justices found that Rebecca Hill, the Colleton County court clerk, had "egregiously attacked" Murdaugh's credibility and swayed the jurors against him.  The court also criticized Hill for her book, "Behind the Doors of Justice: The Murdaugh Murders," which was later unpublished due to plagiarism charges. The state Supreme Court ruled that unrelated evidence, including details about Murdaugh’s financial crimes, was allowed in the trial and will now allow a retrial.  The State Attorney General Alan Wilson plans to retry the case.

articles.title: US man accused of killing rock singer in 1993 arrested after decades on the run | Detroit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Richard Werstine, wanted for the 1993 murder of his friend Rodney Barger, a vocalist with the band Cold as Life, has been apprehended in Panama after spending over 30 years evading authorities.  Werstine was taken into custody at a dog park in Panama City on April 29th following decades as a fugitive. The US Marshals Service took over the case in 2022 and worked with Panamanian authorities to track him down. Officials say Werstine confessed to being on the run from authorities and admitted to entering Panama illegally in 2005.

articles.title: London man shot outside father’s restaurant after family refuses to pay £1 lakh to Turkish gang - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 38-year-old man was shot outside his family's Turkish restaurant in east London after allegedly refusing to pay a £100,000 sum demanded by a feared north London gang. Beytullah Gunduz, who is linked to the "Hackney Turks" gang, is accused of conspiring to murder restaurateur Onur Guzel following a dispute between rival Turkish gangs.  The attack took place outside the family-run Umut 2000 restaurant in Dalston on June 20 last year and left Guzel with life-altering injuries. The alleged gunman, Dogan Over, is believed to have fled to Istanbul after the shooting.

articles.title: Court overturns Alex Murdaugh's murder convictions
articles.rephrased_article: The South Carolina Supreme Court overturned the 2023 murder convictions of Alex Murdaugh, a disgraced lawyer convicted of killing his wife and son. The court ruled that Colleton County Clerk of Court Rebecca Hill unfairly biased the jury against Murdaugh by making comments to jurors during the trial.  Hill has since pleaded guilty to charges related to misconduct in office and obstruction of justice. The justices cited numerous comments made by Hill to jurors, including her telling them not to trust Murdaugh's testimony and urging them to speed up the verdict.

articles.title: Karachi police get 3-day physical remand of alleged cocaine queenpin Anmol alias Pinky - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anmol alias Pinky, an alleged drug supplier, was granted a three-day physical remand by a Karachi court after her arrest in connection with two narcotics cases. The incident sparked controversy when a video surfaced of her being escorted to court without handcuffs.  The investigating officer (IO) filed a revision application against the judicial magistrate's order, arguing that proper interrogation was needed for the investigation. The Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar expressed satisfaction with the police's re-examination of the legal aspects and directed a fair and transparent investigation into the case.

articles.title: 1MDB financier Jho Low seeks pardon from Donald Trump | 1MDB | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jho Low, a fugitive Malaysian financier, has reportedly requested a pardon from President Donald Trump.  Low faces multiple charges in the US and Malaysia related to his alleged role in the misappropriation of at least $4.5 billion from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB). The scandal is one of the world’s biggest financial frauds, with billions plundered from the now defunct sovereign wealth fund. Johari Abdul Ghani, chair of a Malaysian taskforce seeking to recover funds and assets linked to 1MDB, opposes Low's request for a pardon and urges the US to assist Malaysia in locating him.

articles.title: US to impose visa curbs on 13 people linked to Indian firm over prescription pills laced with fentanyl - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has imposed visa restrictions on 13 individuals associated with KS International Traders, an Indian online pharmacy accused of selling counterfeit prescription pills laced with fentanyl. The company, based in Mumbai, generated revenue through trafficking fentanyl, a powerful synthetic opioid that the US government has designated as a "weapon of mass destruction."  This action follows previous sanctions against KS International Traders last year for similar illicit activities.

articles.title: Man booked for using fake number plate on car to evade traffic challans in Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Traffic Police and Attapur police arrested a 28-year-old man, Syed Rizwan Ali, for using a fake vehicle registration plate to evade traffic fines.  Ali affixed the fake plate on his car and used it to avoid generating challans against him. The case was registered under relevant provisions of the e Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act. Police issued a notice to Ali under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

articles.title: Supreme Court to hear ED plea against bail granted to accused in West Bengal coal scam case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) appeal against the grant of anticipatory bail to Anup Majee, accused of leading a coal mining scam in West Bengal. The ED claims that Mr. Majee operated with the “active” assistance of several leaders from the All India Trinamool Congress.  The court sought Mr. Majee’s response to the agency's plea challenging a June 2025 order granting him bail in a money laundering case registered in 2020.

articles.title: Over ₹1 crore cash, AK-47 rifles recovered from Maoist hideouts, say police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Narayanpur district, Chhattisgarh, have recovered over ₹1.01 crore in cash and a significant amount of arms and ammunition, including AK-47 and SLR rifles, from former Maoist hideouts or dumps in the past month.  The largest recovery was made on May 9th at Nelangur village near the Chhattisgarh-Maharashtra border, where ₹84 lakh in cash was found alongside two AK-47 rifles.

articles.title: Honduras mayor arrested for masterminding environmentalist’s killing | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Honduran authorities arrested Adan Funez, former mayor of Tocoa, for allegedly orchestrating the 2024 assassination of environmental activist Juan Lopez.  F Nunez was captured at his home on Tuesday and joins two other suspects, businessman Hector Eduardo Méndez and Juan Angel Ramos Gallegos, who are accused of criminal association to the detriment of fundamental rights. The arrests follow years of accusations against Funez by religious and environmental leaders and come after a string of prior arrests related to Lopez's death.  The trial is set for next June.

articles.title: 'His kids are here, he's being deported': Top LA restaurant owner arrested by ICE after his own worker ratted him out - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Lool, owner of two Los Angeles restaurants, was detained by ICE agents last week while collecting supplies for a catering event. The arrest stemmed from a former employee's claim that a firearm was kept at the restaurant, violating Lool's parole conditions.  Lool, who is originally from Guatemala and has a criminal record dating back to the 1990s, faces deportation as his business partner and girlfriend describe the situation as "devastating" for their family and businesses.
